source.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν πάλιν εἰς συναγωγήν, καὶ ἦν ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπος ἐξηραμμένην ἔχων τὴν χεῖρα.

records.literal_gloss: And he entered again into [the] synagogue, and there was there a man withered having the hand;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered the synagogue again, and a man was there who had a withered hand;
en.B: Once again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the synagogue. A man was there whose hand was withered.
en.R: Another time Jesus went into the synagogue. A man was there who had a dried-up, useless hand.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 다시 회당에 들어가셨는데, 거기에 말라 버린 손을 가진 사람이 있었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 다시 회당에 들어가셨다. 거기에 손이 오그라든 사람이 하나 있었다.
ko.R: 또 한번은 예수께서 회당에 들어가셨다. 거기에 손이 말라서 쓰지 못하는 사람이 있었다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại vào nhà hội, và ở đó có một người có bàn tay bị teo;
vi.B: Ngài lại vào nhà hội. Ở đó có một người bị teo một bàn tay.
vi.R: Một lần khác, Đức Giê-xu vào nhà hội. Ở đó có một người bị tật ở tay: bàn tay ấy khô teo, không cử động được.

es.L: Y entró otra vez en la sinagoga, y había allí un hombre que tenía la mano seca;
es.B: Otra vez entró en la sinagoga. Allí había un hombre que tenía una mano atrofiada.
es.R: En otra ocasión, Jesús entró en la sinagoga. Allí había un hombre que tenía una mano seca, que no podía mover.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra de nouveau dans la synagogue, et il y avait là un homme qui avait la main desséchée ;
fr.B: Une fois encore, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans la synagogue. Il y avait là un homme dont la main était atrophiée.
fr.R: Une autre fois, Jésus est entré dans la synagogue. Il y avait là un homme qui avait une main abîmée : elle était toute sèche, et il ne pouvait plus s’en servir.

sw.L: Na aliingia tena katika sinagogi, na huko palikuwa na mtu mwenye mkono uliokauka;
sw.B: Kwa mara nyingine aliingia katika sinagogi. Huko kulikuwa na mtu ambaye mkono wake ulikuwa umekauka.
sw.R: Siku nyingine Yesu aliingia katika sinagogi. Huko kulikuwa na mtu mwenye mkono uliokauka, usioweza kufanya kazi.

decisions.choice: withered: shrunken and unable to move
decisions.reason: The word means dried up. The hand was wasted and useless, perhaps from birth or from an illness.

decisions.choice: again into the synagogue: most likely the one in Capernaum (1:21)
decisions.reason: "Again" points back to 1:21, though Mark does not name the town.

decisions.choice: withered: a perfect participle, a hand that had become withered
decisions.reason: The form suggests that the hand had once been well. Mark does not say.

decisions.choice: a dried-up, useless hand
decisions.reason: Readable says what "withered" means.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrative honours Jesus with "께서" and -시-, Jesus speaks in the plain style (해라체), people speak to him in 합쇼체, and Mark's historic presents stay present only at Literal ("말씀하신다", "오신다"), through chapter 3
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change (style guide, sections 4 and 7). Literal keeps Mark's present tense in narrative (3:3, 3:4, 3:5, 3:13, 3:20, 3:31-34); Balanced and Readable use the past. Recorded once for the chapter.

decisions.choice: "말라 버린" (L); "오그라든" (B); "말라서 쓰지 못하는" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the perfect participle's sense of a hand that had become withered ("말라 버린"); Balanced says what that looks like in everyday Korean, and Readable adds that the hand was useless, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "bị teo" (withered) (L, B); "bị tật ở tay: bàn tay ấy khô teo, không cử động được" (R)
decisions.reason: "Teo" is the everyday word for a limb that has shrunk and lost its strength; "bại" would mean paralysed, which says less about the shrinking. Readable spells out what the condition was, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}" for Jesus in the narrative; Jesus says "Ta" for himself (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The forms of address the Vietnamese style guide (sections 6-7) sets for the Gospels, as in the Vietnamese John: the narrator speaks of Jesus as "Ngài", with the capital as the reader setting; a pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly "Ngài".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on every separate pronoun for Jesus; none on verb endings or on pronouns joined to a verb
decisions.reason: The rule for Mark set at 1:2, following Romans and Hebrews: where Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ("entró"), there is nothing to capitalise, so the English span on "he" has no counterpart; every pronoun Spanish writes for Jesus (él, lo, le, su, mí, mi, te, tu) carries the span, except one joined to the end of a verb ("tocarlo"). A sentence-initial pronoun is written plain.

decisions.choice: seca (L, R); atrofiada (B); que no podía mover (R)
decisions.reason: Following the meaning decision: the hand had shrunk and could not move. "Seca" keeps the Greek picture; "atrofiada" says the same in current Spanish; Readable adds what it meant for the man.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping Mark’s present tense ("il monte", "il vient", "ils disent"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in the French of John: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where Mark tells a past event in the present (3:3, 3:13, 3:20, 3:31-34). Readable uses the passé composé, the narrative tense of spoken French and of school today.

decisions.choice: the deity_pronoun span on every French pronoun for Jesus, subject "il" included, and on "le", "l’", "lui", "tu", "te", "ta", "tes" (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for Jesus carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and also where French needs an object pronoun the English lacks ("ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}observaient"). A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital, as in John.

decisions.choice: la main desséchée (L); la main atrophiée (B); une main abîmée ... toute sèche (R)
decisions.reason: The word is "dried up", of a limb shrunken and unable to move (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the picture with the traditional "desséchée"; Balanced says "atrophiée", the current word for a shrunken limb; Readable describes it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: uliokauka (dried up)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means dried up, shrunken (m1). "Mkono uliopooza" is the familiar Swahili phrase, but it names paralysis, not the wasting the word describes; "uliokauka" keeps the picture. Readable adds "usioweza kufanya kazi" (that could not work), as the English Readable adds "useless".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yake, wake, kwake, naye)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun, as in English
decisions.reason: As in John: Swahili marks most pronouns for Jesus inside the verb ("aliingia", "wakimvizia"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer setting spans than English in this chapter.

source.text: καὶ παρετήρουν αὐτὸν εἰ τοῖς σάββασιν θεραπεύσει αὐτόν, ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: and they were watching him whether on the Sabbaths he will heal him, so that they might accuse him.

en.L: and they were watching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} closely [to see] whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they might accuse {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They kept a close eye on Jesus to see if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could bring a charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Some people there watched Jesus closely. They wanted to see if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would heal the man on the Sabbath day. If {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did, they could say {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had broken the law.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 그분을 고발하려고, 그분이 안식일에 그 사람을 고치실지 [보려고] 그분을 지켜보고 있었다.
ko.B: 어떤 사람들은 예수께서 안식일에 그 사람을 고치시는지 보려고 예수를 눈여겨 지켜보았다. 예수를 고발할 구실을 찾으려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 거기 있던 어떤 사람들이 예수를 유심히 지켜보았다. 예수께서 안식일에 그 사람을 고쳐 주시는지 보려는 것이었다. 만일 그렇게 하시면, 예수께서 율법을 어기셨다고 고발할 생각이었다.

vi.L: và họ rình xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chữa lành người ấy trong ngày Sa-bát không, để tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Họ theo dõi Đức Giê-xu thật kỹ, xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chữa bệnh cho người ấy trong ngày Sa-bát không, để có cớ tố cáo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Có mấy người ở đó theo dõi Đức Giê-xu rất kỹ. Họ muốn xem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có chữa bệnh cho người ấy trong ngày Sa-bát không. Nếu {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chữa, họ sẽ có cớ nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phạm luật.

es.L: y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} observaban atentamente [para ver] si lo sanaría en sábado, para poder acusar{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}.
es.B: Vigilaban de cerca a Jesús para ver si sanaría al hombre en sábado, y así poder presentar una acusación contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Algunos de los que estaban allí observaban a Jesús con atención. Querían ver si sanaría al hombre en sábado. Si lo hacía, podrían decir que había quebrantado la ley.

fr.L: et ils {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}observaient [pour voir] s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le guérirait le jour du sabbat, afin de {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.
fr.B: Ils surveillaient Jésus de près pour voir s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} guérirait cet homme le jour du sabbat ; ils voulaient avoir de quoi {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accuser.
fr.R: Certaines personnes surveillaient Jésus de près. Elles voulaient voir s’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} allait guérir l’homme le jour du sabbat. Si {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le faisait, elles pourraient dire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait désobéi à la Loi.

sw.L: na walikuwa wakimvizia [waone] kama atamponya siku ya Sabato, ili wapate kumshtaki.
sw.B: Walikuwa wakimvizia Yesu, waone kama angemponya mtu huyo siku ya Sabato, ili wapate sababu ya kumshtaki.
sw.R: Watu fulani pale walikuwa wakimtazama Yesu kwa makini. Walitaka kuona kama angemponya mtu huyo siku ya Sabato. Kama angefanya hivyo, wangeweza kusema amevunja sheria.

decisions.choice: they were watching: the Pharisees, named in 3:6
decisions.reason: Mark does not name them until 3:6, where the Pharisees go out to plot.

decisions.choice: watching closely: watching for a fault
decisions.reason: The verb means to watch carefully, often with hostile intent, as the purpose clause shows.

decisions.choice: heal on the Sabbath: the teachers allowed it only when life was in danger
decisions.reason: Treating the sick counted as work. Jewish teaching later recorded allowed it on the Sabbath only to save a life. A withered hand could wait a day.

decisions.choice: accuse: bring a charge before a court or the elders
decisions.reason: They want a formal charge of breaking the Sabbath, which the law treated as a serious offense (Exodus 31:14).

decisions.choice: they could say he had broken the law
alternatives: so that they might accuse him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the accusation would be.

decisions.choice: [보려고] (to see)
decisions.reason: Korean needs a verb of seeing before the "whether" clause; Literal brackets it, Balanced and Readable write it plainly.

decisions.choice: "rình xem" (L); "theo dõi thật kỹ" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is watching in order to catch a fault. "Rình" carries that hostile sense by itself; Balanced uses the more neutral "theo dõi thật kỹ" and lets "để có cớ tố cáo" show the motive.

decisions.choice: en sábado
decisions.reason: The Greek plural is the usual way of naming the Sabbath day; Spanish "sábado" is the same word and needs no explanation.

decisions.choice: presentar una acusación contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: Says what the meaning decision finds: a formal charge before a court or the elders, and keeps the pronoun for Jesus a separate word.

decisions.choice: le jour du sabbat, lowercase, at every level
decisions.reason: As in the French of John and Colossians: "sabbat" is a common noun in French. The Greek plural is the usual way of naming the day, so Literal too says "le jour du sabbat".

decisions.choice: wakimvizia (they were lying in wait for him)
decisions.reason: The verb means watching closely to find a fault (m2). "Kuvizia" is to watch someone in order to catch them, which says that in one word; Readable uses the plain "wakimtazama kwa makini" (watching closely) and says what they hoped to find.

source.text: καὶ λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τῷ τὴν χεῖρα ἔχοντι ξηράν· Ἔγειρε εἰς τὸ μέσον.

records.literal_gloss: And he says to the man the hand having withered, Rise into the middle.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the man who had the withered hand, "Rise [and come] into the middle."
en.B: Jesus told the man whose hand was withered, "Get up and come out here in front."
en.R: Jesus told the man with the bad hand, "Get up and stand here where everyone can see you."

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 손이 마른 그 사람에게 말씀하신다. "일어나 한가운데로 [나오너라]."
ko.B: 예수께서 손이 오그라든 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나서 이 앞으로 나오너라."
ko.R: 예수께서 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나서 모든 사람이 볼 수 있게 여기 앞에 서라."

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người có bàn tay bị teo: "Hãy đứng dậy [mà ra] giữa [đây]."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu bảo người bị teo tay: "Hãy đứng dậy, ra đứng giữa đây."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu bảo người bị tật ở tay: "Hãy đứng dậy, ra đứng ở đây cho mọi người cùng thấy."

es.L: Y dice al hombre que tenía la mano seca: «Levántate [y ven] al medio».
es.B: Jesús le dijo al hombre de la mano atrofiada: «Levántate y ponte aquí en medio».
es.R: Jesús le dijo al hombre de la mano enferma: «Levántate y ponte aquí, donde todos te puedan ver».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme qui avait la main desséchée : « Lève-toi [et viens] au milieu. »
fr.B: Jésus dit à l’homme à la main atrophiée : « Lève-toi et viens ici, au milieu. »
fr.R: Jésus a dit à l’homme qui avait la main abîmée : « Lève-toi et viens ici, devant tout le monde. »

sw.L: Naye anamwambia yule mtu mwenye mkono uliokauka, "Inuka [uje] katikati."
sw.B: Yesu akamwambia yule mtu mwenye mkono uliokauka, "Simama, uje hapa mbele."
sw.R: Yesu akamwambia yule mtu mwenye mkono mbovu, "Simama, uje hapa mbele ili kila mtu akuone."

decisions.choice: rise into the middle: get up and come where all can see
decisions.reason: Jesus does not heal in secret. He sets the man in the middle of the meeting, in front of those who are watching.

decisions.choice: [and come] (L); come out here in front (B); stand here where everyone can see you (R)
decisions.reason: English needs a verb of motion with "into the middle".

decisions.choice: "{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói" with no "đã" (L), here and wherever Mark tells a past event in the present (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The historic present: Literal keeps it by leaving out the past marker "đã", as the style guide sets; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past.

decisions.choice: present tense kept (L); past tense (B, R): dice / dijo
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense. Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories do. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: [y ven] (L); ponte aquí en medio (B); ponte aquí, donde todos te puedan ver (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the command means getting up and coming where everyone can see (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable (akamwambia)
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present. Literal keeps it, so readers can see it; Balanced and Readable use the narrative past with -ka-, as written Swahili narrative does. This holds for the whole chapter (3:4, 3:5, 3:13, 3:20, 3:31-34).

source.text: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ἀποκτεῖναι;

records.literal_gloss: And he says to them, Is it lawful on the Sabbaths to do good or to do evil, life to save or to kill?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to them, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to kill?"
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What does the law allow on the Sabbath: doing good or doing harm, saving a life or killing?"
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked them, "What does the law say we should do on the Sabbath? Should we do good things or bad things? Should we save a life or kill?"

ko.L: 그리고 그들에게 말씀하신다. "안식일에 허락된 것이 선을 행하는 것이냐, 악을 행하는 것이냐? 목숨을 구하는 것이냐, 죽이는 것이냐?"
ko.B: 그리고 그들에게 물으셨다. "안식일에 율법이 허락하는 것이 무엇이냐? 선한 일을 하는 것이냐, 해를 끼치는 것이냐? 목숨을 살리는 것이냐, 죽이는 것이냐?"
ko.R: 그리고 사람들에게 물으셨다. "안식일에 우리가 무엇을 해야 한다고 율법은 말하느냐? 좋은 일을 해야 하느냐, 나쁜 일을 해야 하느냐? 사람의 목숨을 살려야 하느냐, 죽여야 하느냐?"

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với họ: "Trong ngày Sa-bát, được phép làm điều lành hay làm điều dữ, cứu một mạng người hay giết đi?"
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Trong ngày Sa-bát, luật pháp cho phép làm gì: làm điều tốt hay làm điều ác, cứu mạng người hay giết người?"
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi họ: "Luật pháp dạy chúng ta làm gì trong ngày Sa-bát? Làm điều tốt hay làm điều xấu? Cứu mạng người hay giết người?"

es.L: Y les dice: «¿Es lícito en sábado hacer el bien o hacer el mal, salvar una vida o matar?».
es.B: Luego les preguntó: «¿Qué permite la ley en sábado: hacer el bien o hacer el mal, salvar una vida o matar?».
es.R: Luego les preguntó: «¿Qué dice la ley que debemos hacer en sábado? ¿Hacer el bien o hacer el mal? ¿Salvar una vida o matar?».

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Est-il permis, le jour du sabbat, de faire le bien ou de faire le mal, de sauver une vie ou de tuer ? »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur demanda : « Qu’est-ce que la Loi permet le jour du sabbat : faire le bien ou faire le mal, sauver une vie ou tuer ? »
fr.R: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que la Loi demande de faire le jour du sabbat ? Faut-il faire le bien ou faire le mal ? Faut-il sauver une vie ou tuer ? »

sw.L: Naye anawaambia, "Je, ni halali siku ya Sabato kutenda mema au kutenda mabaya, kuokoa uhai au kuua?"
sw.B: Kisha akawauliza, "Sheria inaruhusu nini siku ya Sabato: kutenda mema au kutenda mabaya, kuokoa maisha ya mtu au kuua?"
sw.R: Kisha akawauliza, "Sheria inasema tufanye nini siku ya Sabato? Tutende mema au tutende mabaya? Tuokoe maisha ya mtu au tuue?"

decisions.choice: do good or do evil: there is no middle way
alternatives: a choice between healing and resting
decisions.reason: Jesus puts the choice so that not doing good, when one can, is doing harm.

decisions.choice: to save a life or to kill: set against their plot (3:6)
decisions.reason: Jesus is about to restore a life on the Sabbath, while they plan that same day how to kill him.

decisions.choice: life: a person, a human life
decisions.reason: The word can mean soul, but here it means a person's life, as in 8:35.

decisions.choice: does the law allow (B); what does the law say (R)
decisions.reason: "Lawful" names what the law of Moses allows. Balanced and Readable say so in plain words.

decisions.choice: "목숨" for psyche (life)
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John, "목숨" is the life a person has and can lose; "생명" is kept for zoe. Here it is a human life that can be saved or taken.

decisions.choice: "mạng người" for psychē
decisions.reason: Here the word means a human life that can be saved or lost. "Mạng người" says exactly that; "linh hồn" (soul) would mislead, and "sự sống" is kept for zōē, as in the Vietnamese John.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué permite la ley ...? (B); ¿Qué dice la ley ...? (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable say whose permission is meant; Literal keeps "es lícito".

decisions.choice: la Loi permet (B); la Loi demande (R)
decisions.reason: As in the English, Balanced and Readable say whose permission is meant: the Law of Moses as the teachers read it. "La Loi" takes a capital, as in John.

decisions.choice: uhai (L); maisha ya mtu (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word here means a person's life (m3). "Roho" would suggest the soul or spirit, so Swahili uses "uhai" (being alive) at Literal and "maisha ya mtu" (a person's life) at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐσιώπων.

records.literal_gloss: They but were silent.

en.L: But they were silent.
en.B: They said nothing.
en.R: But they would not answer.

ko.L: 그러나 그들은 잠잠했다.
ko.B: 그들은 아무 말도 하지 않았다.
ko.R: 그러나 그들은 대답하지 않았다.

vi.L: Nhưng họ im lặng.
vi.B: Họ chẳng nói gì.
vi.R: Nhưng họ không chịu trả lời.

es.L: Pero ellos callaban.
es.B: Ellos no dijeron nada.
es.R: Pero ellos no quisieron responder.

fr.L: Mais eux se taisaient.
fr.B: Ils gardèrent le silence.
fr.R: Mais ils n’ont rien voulu répondre.

sw.L: Lakini wao walinyamaza.
sw.B: Wao hawakusema neno.
sw.R: Lakini hawakutaka kujibu.

decisions.choice: they were silent: they would not answer
decisions.reason: The verb is continuous: they kept silent, refusing to answer.

source.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος αὐτοὺς μετ’ ὀργῆς, συλλυπούμενος ἐπὶ τῇ πωρώσει τῆς καρδίας αὐτῶν, λέγει τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρα· καὶ ἐξέτεινεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardness of the heart of them, he says to the man, Stretch out the hand; and he stretched out, and was restored the hand of him.

en.L: And looking around at them with anger, grieved at the hardness of their heart, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to the man, "Stretch out [your] hand." And he stretched [it] out, and his hand was restored.
en.B: He looked around at them in anger, deeply grieved that their hearts were so hard, and said to the man, "Hold out your hand." He held it out, and it was made well again.
en.R: Jesus looked around at them, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was angry. He was very sad because they did not want to understand. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the man, "Hold out your hand." The man held it out, and his hand was healed. It was as good as new.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 분노하시며 그들을 둘러보시고, 그들 마음의 완고함을 몹시 슬퍼하시면서, 그 사람에게 말씀하신다. "손을 내밀어라." 그러자 그가 내밀었고, 그의 손이 회복되었다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 노하셔서 그들을 둘러보시고, 그들의 마음이 굳어 있는 것을 몹시 슬퍼하시며 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "손을 내밀어라." 그가 손을 내밀자, 그 손이 다시 성하게 되었다.
ko.R: 예수께서 그들을 둘러보셨다. 예수께서는 화가 나셨다. 그들이 하나님의 뜻을 깨달으려 하지 않아서 몹시 마음이 아프셨다. 그리고 그 사람에게 말씀하셨다. "손을 내밀어라." 그 사람이 손을 내밀자, 손이 나았다. 손이 전과 똑같이 멀쩡해졌다.

vi.L: Và nhìn quanh họ với cơn giận, buồn rầu vì lòng họ cứng cỏi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với người ấy: "Hãy giơ tay ra." Và người ấy giơ ra, và tay người ấy được phục hồi.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu giận dữ nhìn quanh họ, đau buồn vì lòng họ quá cứng cỏi, rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo người ấy: "Hãy giơ tay ra." Người ấy giơ tay ra, và tay người ấy được lành lại như trước.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn quanh họ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận. Ngài rất buồn vì họ không muốn hiểu. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo người ấy: "Hãy giơ tay ra." Người ấy giơ tay ra, và bàn tay được chữa lành. Nó lại lành lặn như trước.

es.L: Y mirándolos a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor con ira, entristecido por la dureza de su corazón, dice al hombre: «Extiende la mano». Y [la] extendió, y su mano fue restablecida.
es.B: Paseó la mirada sobre ellos con enojo, profundamente entristecido porque tenían el corazón tan endurecido, y le dijo al hombre: «Extiende la mano». El hombre la extendió, y la mano le quedó sana de nuevo.
es.R: Jesús los miró a todos, y estaba enojado. Le dolía mucho que no quisieran entender. Entonces le dijo al hombre: «Extiende la mano». El hombre la extendió, y su mano quedó sana. Estaba como nueva.

fr.L: Et, les ayant regardés tout autour avec colère, attristé de l’endurcissement de leur cœur, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à l’homme : « Étends la main. » Et il [l’]étendit, et sa main fut rétablie.
fr.B: Il promena sur eux un regard de colère, profondément attristé par la dureté de leur cœur, et dit à l’homme : « Tends la main. » L’homme la tendit, et sa main redevint saine.
fr.R: Jésus a regardé tous ces gens autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était en colère. Il était très triste parce qu’ils refusaient de comprendre. Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit à l’homme : « Tends ta main. » L’homme l’a tendue, et sa main a été guérie. Elle était de nouveau comme avant.

sw.L: Naye akiisha kuwatazama pande zote kwa hasira, akihuzunika kwa sababu ya ugumu wa moyo wao, anamwambia yule mtu, "Nyoosha mkono [wako]." Naye akaunyoosha, na mkono wake ukarejeshwa.
sw.B: Akawatazama pande zote kwa hasira, akihuzunika sana kwa sababu mioyo yao ilikuwa migumu, akamwambia yule mtu, "Nyoosha mkono wako." Akaunyoosha, nao ukapona, ukawa mzima tena.
sw.R: Yesu aliwatazama wote kwa hasira. Alihuzunika sana kwa sababu hawakutaka kuelewa. Kisha akamwambia yule mtu, "Nyoosha mkono wako." Mtu yule akaunyoosha, na mkono wake ukapona. Ukawa mzima kabisa kama zamani.

decisions.choice: with anger: Jesus is angry at their hard hearts
decisions.reason: Mark names Jesus' anger openly. It is joined with grief: he is angry and sad at the same time.

decisions.choice: hardness of heart: a mind closed to God's will
decisions.reason: The heart is the place of thought and will. A hard heart will not understand or respond (6:52; 8:17).

decisions.choice: was restored: made as it had been before
decisions.reason: The word means put back to its former state, which fits a hand that had withered (3:1).

decisions.choice: stretch out your hand: the cure comes by Jesus' word alone
decisions.reason: Jesus does no work that could be charged as Sabbath-breaking; he only speaks.

decisions.choice: they did not want to understand
decisions.reason: Readable says what a hard heart means here.

decisions.choice: "마음의 완고함" (L); "마음이 굳어 있는 것" (B); "하나님의 뜻을 깨달으려 하지 않아서" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun; Balanced keeps the picture of a hardened heart in plain Korean; Readable says what it means, following the meaning decision (a mind closed to God's will).

decisions.choice: "lòng họ cứng cỏi" for the hardness of their heart
decisions.reason: "Lòng cứng cỏi" keeps the picture of the heart and is the phrase the Vietnamese John uses at 12:40 (Readable); "chai đá" adds the idea of cruelty.

decisions.choice: Extiende la mano, with no possessive
decisions.reason: Spanish names a part of the body with the article, so it needs no word for English "your" and nothing is supplied. Literal brackets only "[la]" in the reply, which the Greek leaves out.

decisions.choice: porque tenían el corazón tan endurecido
alternatives: por la dureza de su corazón
decisions.reason: "Su corazón" could be read as Jesus's heart; Balanced says plainly that the hardness was theirs. Literal keeps the Greek phrase.

decisions.choice: l’endurcissement de leur cœur (L); la dureté de leur cœur (B)
decisions.reason: The word is a hardening, a mind closed to God’s will (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the noun of process; Balanced says the state in a familiar French phrase. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: ugumu wa moyo wao (L); mioyo yao ilikuwa migumu (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek singular "heart" for the group; Balanced uses the plural "mioyo", which is the natural Swahili for many people. Both keep the picture of a hard heart, a mind closed to God's will (m2), rather than replacing it with "ukaidi" (stubbornness).

source.text: καὶ ἐξελθόντες οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εὐθὺς μετὰ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν συμβούλιον ἐδίδουν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone out the Pharisees immediately with the Herodians counsel were giving against him, how him they might destroy.

en.L: And the Pharisees went out and immediately began to take counsel with the Herodians against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, how they might destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees left, and at once they began making plans with the Herodians about how to destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then the Pharisees left. Right away they met with the people who supported King Herod, and they made plans to kill Jesus.

ko.L: 그리고 바리새파 사람들은 나가서 곧 헤롯 당원들과 함께, 어떻게 하면 그분을 없앨 수 있을지 그분을 거슬러 의논하기 시작했다.
ko.B: 바리새파 사람들은 나가서 곧바로 헤롯 당원들과 함께 어떻게 예수를 없앨지 모의하기 시작했다.
ko.R: 그러자 바리새파 사람들이 회당에서 나갔다. 그들은 바로 헤롯 왕을 따르는 사람들과 만나서, 예수를 죽일 계획을 세웠다.

vi.L: Và người Pha-ri-si đi ra, lập tức bàn mưu với những người thuộc phe Hê-rốt chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, làm sao để tiêu diệt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Người Pha-ri-si đi ra, và ngay lập tức họ bắt đầu bàn mưu với phe Hê-rốt, tìm cách giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Rồi người Pha-ri-si bỏ ra về. Ngay lúc ấy, họ họp với những người ủng hộ vua Hê-rốt và bàn mưu giết Đức Giê-xu.

es.L: Y los fariseos salieron, y enseguida comenzaron a tomar consejo con los herodianos contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, sobre cómo {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} destruirían.
es.B: Los fariseos salieron, y enseguida comenzaron a tramar con los herodianos cómo acabar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Entonces los fariseos salieron. Enseguida se reunieron con los partidarios del rey Herodes, e hicieron planes para matar a Jesús.

fr.L: Et les Pharisiens, étant sortis, se mirent aussitôt à tenir conseil avec les Hérodiens contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, sur la manière de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire périr.
fr.B: Les Pharisiens sortirent et se concertèrent aussitôt avec les Hérodiens sur le moyen de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir.
fr.R: Alors les Pharisiens sont sortis. Tout de suite, ils se sont réunis avec les partisans du roi Hérode, et ils ont cherché un moyen de tuer Jésus.

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo walitoka, na mara wakaanza kufanya shauri pamoja na watu wa Herode dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, jinsi ya kumwangamiza.
sw.B: Mafarisayo walitoka, na mara moja wakaanza kupanga shauri pamoja na wafuasi wa Herode jinsi ya kumwangamiza Yesu.
sw.R: Kisha Mafarisayo waliondoka. Mara moja walikutana na watu waliomuunga mkono Mfalme Herode, wakapanga njama ya kumuua Yesu.

decisions.choice: the Herodians: supporters of Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee
decisions.reason: They backed Herod's family and Roman rule. Pharisees and Herodians did not usually work together; they join against Jesus again in 12:13.

decisions.choice: destroy: put to death
decisions.reason: The verb means to kill, as in 11:18. This is the first plot against his life in Mark.

decisions.choice: were taking counsel: they began to plot
decisions.reason: The phrase means to form a plan together.

decisions.choice: the people who supported King Herod
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the Herodians were. Herod Antipas was called king (6:14).

decisions.choice: "헤롯 당원들" (L, B); "헤롯 왕을 따르는 사람들" (R)
decisions.reason: "헤롯 당원" is the established Protestant term for the Herodians; Readable says who they were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "곧" (L); "곧바로" (B); "바로" (R) for euthys, through chapter 3
decisions.reason: Mark's frequent "immediately" keeps one Korean word per level so the pace of his telling stays visible; "즉시" sounds administrative in narrative.

decisions.choice: "phe Hê-rốt" for the Herodians
decisions.reason: "Phe" names a party of supporters without the modern political sense of "đảng"; "Hê-rốt" is the Protestant form of the name. Readable says who they were, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: enseguida
decisions.reason: Mark's word for moving the story straight on; "enseguida" at every level here, as in 1:10.

decisions.choice: los partidarios del rey Herodes
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says who the Herodians were (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: les Hérodiens (L, B); les partisans du roi Hérode (R)
decisions.reason: "Hérodiens" is the usual French form, capitalised like "les Pharisiens" in the French style guide; Readable says who they were, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: le faire périr (L); le faire mourir (B)
decisions.reason: The verb means to put to death here (meaning decision m2). "Perdre" in this sense is now old-fashioned; Literal keeps the strong verb "périr", Balanced says plainly "faire mourir", as John 5:18 does.

decisions.choice: watu wa Herode (L); wafuasi wa Herode (B); watu waliomuunga mkono Mfalme Herode (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no settled word for the Herodians. A borrowed "Maherodia" would mean nothing to most readers, so Literal says "Herod's people", which is what the Greek name means, Balanced "Herod's followers" and Readable "the people who supported King Herod", as the English Readable does (m1). For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: mara (L); mara moja (B, R) for "immediately"
decisions.reason: Mark's frequent "immediately" is "mara" at Literal and the fuller "mara moja" (at once) at Balanced and Readable, throughout the chapter.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἀνεχώρησεν πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ πολὺ πλῆθος ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἠκολούθησεν, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰδουμαίας καὶ πέραν τοῦ Ἰορδάνου καὶ περὶ Τύρον καὶ Σιδῶνα, πλῆθος πολύ, ἀκούοντες ὅσα ἐποίει ἦλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And the Jesus with the disciples of him withdrew to the sea, and a great multitude from the Galilee followed, and from the Judea \v 8 and from Jerusalem and from the Idumea and beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon, a multitude great, hearing how much he was doing, came to him.

en.L: And Jesus withdrew with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to the sea, and a great multitude from Galilee followed, and from Judea \v 8 and from Jerusalem and from Idumea and beyond the Jordan and around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, hearing all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Jesus went off with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to the lake, and a large crowd from Galilee followed. \v 8 Hearing about all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing, a great many people also came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from Judea and Jerusalem, from Idumea and the land beyond the Jordan, and from the area around Tyre and Sidon.
en.R: Jesus went away to Lake Galilee with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers. A large crowd of people from Galilee followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 8 Many others heard about all the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing. They came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the lands of Judea and Idumea, from the city of Jerusalem, from the other side of the Jordan River, and from the area around the cities of Tyre and Sidon.

ko.L: 그리고 예수께서 그분의 제자들과 함께 바다 쪽으로 물러가셨다. 그러자 갈릴리에서 큰 무리가 따라왔고, 또 유대에서, \v 8 예루살렘에서, 이두매에서, 요단 강 건너편에서, 두로와 시돈 근방에서도 큰 무리가 그분이 하시는 모든 일을 듣고 그분께 왔다.
ko.B: 예수께서 제자들과 함께 바닷가로 물러가셨다. 그러자 갈릴리에서 많은 사람이 따라왔다. \v 8 또 예수께서 하시는 모든 일을 전해 듣고, 유대와 예루살렘, 이두매와 요단 강 건너편, 그리고 두로와 시돈 근방에서도 많은 사람이 예수께 몰려왔다.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들과 함께 갈릴리 호숫가로 가셨다. 갈릴리에서 온 많은 사람이 예수를 따라왔다. \v 8 다른 많은 사람들도 예수께서 하시는 일을 모두 전해 들었다. 그래서 유대 지방과 이두매 지방에서, 예루살렘 도시에서, 요단 강 건너편에서, 그리고 두로와 시돈이라는 도시들 근처에서도 사람들이 예수께 왔다.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu cùng với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lui về phía biển; và một đoàn người đông đảo từ Ga-li-lê đi theo, và từ Giu-đê \v 8 và từ Giê-ru-sa-lem và từ Y-đu-mê và bên kia [sông] Giô-đanh và vùng quanh Ty-rơ và Si-đôn, một đoàn người đông đảo, nghe những việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang làm, đã đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu cùng các môn đồ lui về phía hồ, và một đoàn dân đông từ Ga-li-lê đi theo. \v 8 Nghe biết mọi việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang làm, rất nhiều người khác cũng kéo đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ Giu-đê và Giê-ru-sa-lem, từ Y-đu-mê và miền bên kia sông Giô-đanh, và từ vùng chung quanh Ty-rơ và Si-đôn.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đi đến hồ Ga-li-lê với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Một đám đông rất lớn từ miền Ga-li-lê đi theo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \v 8 Nhiều người khác nghe về mọi việc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm. Họ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từ miền Giu-đê và miền Y-đu-mê, từ thành Giê-ru-sa-lem, từ bên kia sông Giô-đanh, và từ vùng quanh các thành Ty-rơ và Si-đôn.

es.L: Y Jesús se retiró con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos hacia el mar, y una gran multitud de Galilea [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] siguió, y de Judea \v 8 y de Jerusalén y de Idumea y del otro lado del Jordán y de los alrededores de Tiro y Sidón, una gran multitud, al oír cuántas cosas hacía, vino a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Jesús se retiró con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos hacia el lago, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió una gran multitud de Galilea. \v 8 Al oír todo lo que hacía, también vino a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} muchísima gente de Judea y de Jerusalén, de Idumea y de la región al otro lado del Jordán, y de los alrededores de Tiro y Sidón.
es.R: Jesús se fue con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos al lago de Galilea. Una gran multitud de Galilea {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió. \v 8 Muchos otros oyeron hablar de todo lo que hacía. Llegaron hasta {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} desde las regiones de Judea e Idumea, desde la ciudad de Jerusalén, desde el otro lado del río Jordán y desde los alrededores de las ciudades de Tiro y Sidón.

fr.L: Et Jésus se retira avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples vers la mer ; et une grande multitude de la Galilée [{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}] suivit, et de la Judée \v 8 et de Jérusalem et de l’Idumée et d’au-delà du Jourdain et des environs de Tyr et de Sidon, une grande multitude, entendant tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait, vint à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Jésus se retira avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples au bord de la mer, et une grande foule venue de Galilée {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivit. \v 8 Apprenant tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait, une foule nombreuse vint aussi à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} de Judée et de Jérusalem, d’Idumée et de l’autre rive du Jourdain, et de la région de Tyr et de Sidon.
fr.R: Jésus est parti au bord du lac avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples. Une grande foule de gens de Galilée {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a suivi. \v 8 Beaucoup d’autres ont entendu parler de tout ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait. Ils sont venus {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trouver depuis la Judée et l’Idumée, depuis la ville de Jérusalem, depuis l’autre côté du Jourdain et depuis la région des villes de Tyr et de Sidon.

sw.L: Na Yesu alijiondoa pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwenda baharini; na umati mkubwa kutoka Galilaya ukafuata, na kutoka Uyahudi \v 8 na kutoka Yerusalemu na kutoka Idumaya na ng'ambo ya Yordani na kandokando ya Tiro na Sidoni, umati mkubwa, waliposikia mambo yote aliyokuwa akiyafanya, walikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Yesu aliondoka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaenda ziwani, na umati mkubwa wa watu kutoka Galilaya ukawafuata. \v 8 Watu wengi sana pia walisikia habari za mambo yote aliyokuwa akiyafanya, wakaja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} kutoka Uyahudi na Yerusalemu, kutoka Idumaya na nchi ya ng'ambo ya Yordani, na kutoka maeneo ya kandokando ya Tiro na Sidoni.
sw.R: Yesu aliondoka pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, wakaenda kwenye Ziwa Galilaya. Umati mkubwa wa watu kutoka Galilaya ukamfuata. \v 8 Watu wengine wengi walisikia habari za mambo yote aliyokuwa akiyafanya. Walikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} kutoka nchi za Uyahudi na Idumaya, kutoka mji wa Yerusalemu, kutoka ng'ambo ya Mto Yordani, na kutoka maeneo ya kandokando ya miji ya Tiro na Sidoni.

decisions.choice: withdrew: went away, out of danger
decisions.reason: After the plot of 3:6 Jesus leaves the town for the lakeshore.

decisions.choice: the places: Jewish lands to the south and east, Gentile cities to the north
decisions.reason: Judea and Jerusalem lay far south. Idumea, old Edom, lay south of Judea. Beyond the Jordan lay Perea. Tyre and Sidon were Gentile cities on the coast to the north-west.

decisions.choice: the crowd from Galilee followed; another great crowd came from farther away
alternatives: one crowd from all these places followed him
decisions.reason: The Greek names a great multitude twice. The second, from the other regions, came because they heard what he was doing.

decisions.choice: the places listed after "came to him" (B); split into sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the long list at the end of the sentence so that the verb is not lost.

decisions.choice: "바다" (L, B); "갈릴리 호수" (R) for the Sea of Galilee, through Mark
decisions.reason: "바다" is the established Korean name ("갈릴리 바다") and keeps Mark's word; Readable calls it a lake, which is what it is, as the Korean John does at 6:1 and 21:1.

decisions.choice: Protestant place names: "이두매", "요단 강", "두로", "시돈"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (style guide, section 5); the Catholic and Common Translation forms are the alternatives.

decisions.choice: "biển" (L); "hồ" (B); "hồ Ga-li-lê" (R) for the Sea of Galilee (whole book)
decisions.reason: Mark calls the lake "the sea". Literal keeps his word; Balanced and Readable say what it is, a freshwater lake, as the English does. The Vietnamese John keeps "biển Ga-li-lê" as the place name (6:1), which a reader may meet alongside.

decisions.choice: Y-đu-mê, Ty-rơ, Si-đôn, Giô-đanh
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliterations, as the style guide settles for names.

decisions.choice: discípulos at every level
decisions.reason: As the Spanish of John does, "discípulos" is kept at Readable too: it is a plain word in Spanish, and the English "followers" says the same thing. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B); el lago de Galilea (R)
decisions.reason: Mark calls the lake of Galilee a sea. Literal keeps his word; Balanced and Readable say what it was, as the English does.

decisions.choice: [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] siguió
decisions.reason: The Greek verb has no object; Spanish "seguir" needs one, so Literal supplies it in brackets.

decisions.choice: la mer (L, B); le lac (R) (for the whole chapter and the next)
decisions.reason: As in the French of John (6:16): Literal and Balanced keep "la mer", the Greek word and the usual French name ("la mer de Galilée"); Readable says "le lac" so young readers do not picture the ocean. The English Balanced says "lake"; French Balanced follows the French usage already set in John.

decisions.choice: disciples at every level, Readable included
decisions.reason: The French style guide keeps "disciples" at every level; the word is plain in French.

decisions.choice: bahari (L); ziwa (B); Ziwa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: Mark calls the lake of Galilee "the sea". Literal keeps "bahari" (sea); Balanced says "ziwa" (lake), which is what it is, and Readable names it, as the English does with "lake" and "Lake Galilee". John 6:1 keeps the name "Bahari ya Galilaya"; here no name is given. This holds wherever Mark says "the sea" for the lake.

decisions.choice: Uyahudi (Judea); Idumaya (Idumea)
decisions.reason: "Uyahudi" is the name John uses for Judea (John 7:3; 11:7), so the Gospels agree; Idumea is given its usual Swahili form "Idumaya".

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα πλοιάριον προσκαρτερῇ αὐτῷ διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μὴ θλίβωσιν αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to the disciples of him that a small boat might stand ready for him because of the crowd, so that not they might crush him;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples that a small boat should stand ready for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because of the crowd, so that they would not crush {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}};
en.B: Because of the crowd, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples to keep a small boat ready for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not be crushed.
en.R: There were so many people that Jesus told {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers to have a small boat ready for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Then the crowd would not push against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and crush {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 그분의 제자들에게, 무리 때문에 작은 배 한 척을 자기를 위해 대기시켜 두라고 말씀하셨다. 무리가 자기를 짓누르지 않게 하려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 무리 때문에 제자들에게 작은 배 한 척을 준비해 두라고 이르셨다. 사람들에게 떠밀려 짓눌리지 않으시려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 사람들이 너무 많았다. 그래서 예수께서는 제자들에게 작은 배 한 척을 준비해 두라고 말씀하셨다. 사람들이 몰려와서 예수를 밀어 대지 못하게 하려는 것이었다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} rằng một chiếc thuyền nhỏ phải luôn sẵn sàng cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì đám đông, để họ khỏi chen ép {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}};
vi.B: Vì dân chúng quá đông, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bảo các môn đồ giữ sẵn một chiếc thuyền nhỏ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} khỏi bị họ chen ép.
vi.R: Vì có quá nhiều người, Đức Giê-xu bảo các môn đồ chuẩn bị sẵn một chiếc thuyền nhỏ cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Như vậy, đám đông sẽ không xô đẩy và chen ép {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

es.L: Y dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que una barca pequeña estuviera lista para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a causa de la multitud, para que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aplastaran;
es.B: A causa de la multitud, les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tuvieran lista una barca pequeña, para que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aplastaran.
es.R: Había tanta gente que Jesús les dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos que tuvieran lista una barca pequeña para {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Así la gente no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} empujaría ni {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} aplastaría.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples qu’une petite barque se tienne prête pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} à cause de la foule, afin qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écrasent pas ;
fr.B: À cause de la foule, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} tenir une petite barque prête, pour ne pas être écrasé.
fr.R: Il y avait tellement de monde que Jésus a demandé à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} préparer une petite barque. Ainsi, la foule ne pourrait pas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} bousculer et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}écraser.

sw.L: Naye akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwamba mashua ndogo imngojee kwa sababu ya umati, wasije wakamsonga;
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya umati wa watu, aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wamwekee tayari mashua ndogo, ili watu wasimsonge.
sw.R: Watu walikuwa wengi sana, kwa hiyo Yesu aliwaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wamwandalie mashua ndogo. Hivyo umati usingemsukuma na kumbana.

decisions.choice: a small boat ready: so that he could step away from the shore
decisions.reason: The boat lets him teach from the water (4:1) and escape the press of the crowd.

decisions.choice: crush: press hard upon him
decisions.reason: The crowd is not hostile, only so many that they could crush him.

decisions.choice: barca pequeña
decisions.reason: "Barca" is the usual Spanish word for a fishing boat on the lake; "pequeña" renders the diminutive.

source.text: πολλοὺς γὰρ ἐθεράπευσεν, ὥστε ἐπιπίπτειν αὐτῷ ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψωνται ὅσοι εἶχον μάστιγας.

records.literal_gloss: many for he healed, so that to fall upon him so that him they might touch, as many as were having diseases.

en.L: for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had healed many, so that all who had diseases were falling upon {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} so that they might touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He had healed many, and so all who had diseases kept pushing forward to touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: He had healed many people. So everyone who was sick was pushing toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, trying to touch {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

ko.L: 그분이 많은 사람을 고치셨으므로, 병에 시달리는 사람은 누구나 그분을 만지려고 그분께로 덮치듯 몰려들었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 많은 사람을 고쳐 주셨기 때문에, 병을 앓는 사람들이 모두 예수께 손을 대려고 밀려들었다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 많은 사람을 고쳐 주셨다. 그래서 아픈 사람들은 모두 예수를 만지려고 예수께 밀고 들어왔다.

vi.L: vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chữa lành nhiều người, đến nỗi tất cả những ai mắc bệnh tật đều đổ xô vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để sờ đến {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Ngài đã chữa lành nhiều người, nên tất cả những ai mắc bệnh đều chen lấn đến để sờ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Ngài đã chữa lành cho nhiều người. Vì vậy, mọi người bệnh đều chen lên phía {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, cố sờ vào {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

es.L: porque había sanado a muchos, de modo que todos los que tenían aflicciones se echaban sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para tocarlo.
es.B: Había sanado a muchos, así que todos los que sufrían enfermedades se abalanzaban sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para tocarlo.
es.R: Había sanado a mucha gente. Por eso todos los enfermos empujaban para llegar hasta {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y tocarlo.

fr.L: car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} en avait guéri beaucoup, de sorte que tous ceux qui avaient des maux se jetaient sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher.
fr.B: Il avait guéri beaucoup de gens, si bien que tous ceux qui souffraient de maladies se pressaient contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher.
fr.R: Il avait guéri beaucoup de gens. Alors tous les malades se poussaient vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour essayer de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} toucher.

sw.L: kwa maana alikuwa amewaponya wengi, hata wote waliokuwa na maradhi walikuwa wakimsongea ili wamguse.
sw.B: Alikuwa amewaponya watu wengi, kwa hiyo wote waliokuwa na maradhi walikuwa wakimsongea ili wamguse.
sw.R: Alikuwa amewaponya watu wengi. Kwa hiyo kila mgonjwa alikuwa akisukumana ili amkaribie, akijaribu kumgusa.

decisions.choice: diseases: afflictions, literally whips or scourges
decisions.reason: The word means a whip, and is used for painful illnesses (5:29, 34).

decisions.choice: to touch him: they believed his touch would heal
decisions.reason: The woman in 5:27-28 and the people in 6:56 do the same.

decisions.choice: falling upon: pressing against him
decisions.reason: The verb pictures people crowding into him, not bowing.

decisions.choice: "병에 시달리는" for mastix
decisions.reason: The Greek word is literally a whip; "시달리다" (be tormented) keeps the sense of a painful affliction without a picture Korean readers would not follow.

decisions.choice: "bệnh tật" for the afflictions (literally "whips")
decisions.reason: The Greek pictures illness as a scourge; Vietnamese has no word with both senses, so all levels say "bệnh" and the meaning decision keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: aflicciones (L); enfermedades (B); los enfermos (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means whips, and so painful afflictions (meaning decision m1). "Azotes" would be read as beatings; "aflicciones" keeps the sense of suffering for Literal.

decisions.choice: des maux (L)
decisions.reason: The word means whips or scourges, used of painful diseases (meaning decision m1). "Fléaux" would suggest public calamities; "maux" is the plain French word for afflictions and still sounds like suffering.

decisions.choice: wakimsongea (pressing towards him)
decisions.reason: The Greek says the sick were "falling upon" him, that is, pressing against him (m3). "Kumwangukia mtu" in Swahili usually means falling at someone's feet to beg, so Literal and Balanced say "wakimsongea", pressing in on him.

source.text: καὶ τὰ πνεύματα τὰ ἀκάθαρτα, ὅταν αὐτὸν ἐθεώρουν, προσέπιπτον αὐτῷ καὶ ἔκραζον λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the spirits the unclean, whenever him they were seeing, were falling down before him and crying out saying, You are the Son of the God.

en.L: And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, would fall down before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and cry out, saying, "You are the Son of God."
en.B: Whenever the unclean spirits saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they threw themselves down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and shouted, "You are the Son of God!"
en.R: When people with evil spirits saw Jesus, the spirits made them fall down in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. The spirits shouted, "You are the Son of God!"

ko.L: 그리고 더러운 영들은 그분을 볼 때마다 그분 앞에 엎드리며 소리 질러 말했다. "당신은 하나님의 아들입니다."
ko.B: 더러운 영들은 예수를 볼 때마다 예수 앞에 엎드려 외쳤다. "당신은 하나님의 아들이십니다!"
ko.R: 악한 영이 들린 사람들은 예수를 보면, 그 영 때문에 예수 앞에 엎드렸다. 그리고 그 영들은 "당신은 하나님의 아들이십니다!" 하고 소리쳤다.

vi.L: Và các tà linh ô uế, hễ khi nào thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì sấp mình xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và kêu lên rằng: "Ngài là Con Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Mỗi khi các tà linh ô uế thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, chúng sấp mình xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và la lớn: "Ngài là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"
vi.R: Khi những người bị tà linh ám thấy Đức Giê-xu, các tà linh khiến họ ngã xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Các tà linh la lên: "Ngài là Con Đức Chúa Trời!"

es.L: Y los espíritus impuros, cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veían, se postraban ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y gritaban diciendo: «Tú eres el Hijo de Dios».
es.B: Cada vez que los espíritus impuros {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} veían, se arrojaban al suelo delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y gritaban: «¡Tú eres el Hijo de Dios!».
es.R: Cuando las personas que tenían espíritus malos veían a Jesús, los espíritus las hacían caer al suelo delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Los espíritus gritaban: «¡Tú eres el Hijo de Dios!».

fr.L: Et les esprits impurs, quand ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyaient, tombaient devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et criaient en disant : « Tu es le Fils de Dieu. »
fr.B: Chaque fois que les esprits impurs {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voyaient, ils se jetaient à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds en criant : « Tu es le Fils de Dieu ! »
fr.R: Quand des gens qui avaient des esprits mauvais voyaient Jésus, les esprits les faisaient tomber devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils criaient : « Tu es le Fils de Dieu ! »

sw.L: Na roho wachafu, kila walipomwona, walikuwa wakianguka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kupaza sauti, wakisema, "Wewe ni Mwana wa Mungu."
sw.B: Kila mara roho wachafu walipomwona, walijitupa chini mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na kupiga kelele, "Wewe ni Mwana wa Mungu!"
sw.R: Watu waliokuwa na roho waovu walipomwona Yesu, roho hao waliwaangusha chini mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Roho hao walipiga kelele, "Wewe ni Mwana wa Mungu!"

decisions.choice: the Son of God: the title God gave at the baptism (1:11)
alternatives: a son of God like any good person
decisions.reason: The spirits know what the crowds do not. A Roman centurion says it at the cross (15:39).

decisions.choice: whenever ... would fall: it happened again and again
decisions.reason: The verbs describe repeated action.

decisions.choice: fall down before him: the spirits bow, but the men they control fall
decisions.reason: The spirits act through the people they hold. Falling down is not worship but submission to one stronger (3:27).

decisions.choice: people with evil spirits; the spirits made them fall
decisions.reason: Readable shows that it was the people who fell, under the spirits' power.

decisions.choice: "더러운 영" (L, B); "악한 영" (R) for the unclean spirits
decisions.reason: "더러운 영" keeps Mark's word "unclean", which is about ritual impurity set against the Holy Spirit; Readable says "악한 영" (evil spirit), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: The spirits address Jesus in 합쇼체 with "당신"
decisions.reason: The spirits bow and name him truly, so they speak up to him; "당신" keeps the stressed "you" of the Greek. A reviewer may prefer the plain style for hostile spirits.

decisions.choice: "tà linh ô uế" (L, B); "tà linh" (R) for the unclean spirits, and "chúng" for them (whole book)
decisions.reason: "Tà linh" is the plain modern Protestant word for an evil spirit; "ô uế" keeps Mark's "unclean", the ritual impurity that set them against the holy. "Tà ma" is the older wording, "thần ô uế" the Catholic one. "Chúng" is the ordinary pronoun for hostile beings.

decisions.choice: "Ngài" for "you" when the spirits address Jesus
decisions.reason: The spirits know who he is and say so; Vietnamese marks that with the reverent "Ngài". It begins the sentence, so it is written plainly with its capital.

decisions.choice: espíritus impuros (L, B); espíritus malos (R)
decisions.reason: "Inmundo" is the traditional word but now sounds like dirt. "Impuro" keeps the sense of what is unfit to come near God; Readable says plainly that the spirits are evil, as the English does.

decisions.choice: las personas que tenían espíritus malos; los espíritus las hacían caer
decisions.reason: As in English: the spirits bow, but it is the people they control who fall (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: les esprits impurs (L, B); des esprits mauvais (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Impur" keeps the language of ritual purity that the Greek word carries; "immonde" is old and now means disgusting. Readable says "mauvais", the plain word, as the English Readable says "evil".

decisions.choice: Tu es le Fils de Dieu, with no span
decisions.reason: The pronoun addressed to Jesus opens the quoted sentence, so it is written plainly with its capital, as the French style guide sets out.

decisions.choice: roho wachafu (L, B); roho waovu (R)
decisions.reason: "Roho" with the personal agreement used for living beings (roho wachafu, walipomwona) names the unclean spirits; "pepo" is kept for the Greek word for demons (3:15, 3:22), as in John 8:48. Readable says "roho waovu" (evil spirits), as the English Readable says "evil spirits". For the whole book.

source.text: καὶ πολλὰ ἐπετίμα αὐτοῖς ἵνα μὴ αὐτὸν φανερὸν ποιήσωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And much he was rebuking them, so that not him known they might make.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would strongly rebuke them, so that they would not make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known.
en.B: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sternly ordered them not to make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known.
en.R: But Jesus strongly warned them not to tell people who {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was.

ko.L: 그러면 그분은 그들이 자기를 드러내지 못하도록 그들을 엄하게 꾸짖곤 하셨다.
ko.B: 그러나 예수께서는 자기를 알리지 말라고 그들에게 엄하게 명령하셨다.
ko.R: 그러나 예수께서는 자기가 누구인지 사람들에게 말하지 말라고 그 영들에게 엄하게 경고하셨다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} quở trách chúng rất nghiêm, để chúng đừng làm cho người ta biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghiêm khắc ra lệnh cho chúng không được tiết lộ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là ai.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu nghiêm khắc cấm chúng nói cho người ta biết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là ai.

es.L: Y les reprendía mucho para que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dieran a conocer.
es.B: Pero les ordenaba severamente que no {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} dieran a conocer.
es.R: Pero Jesús les advertía con firmeza que no dijeran a nadie quién era {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les réprimandait sévèrement, afin qu’ils ne {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} fassent pas connaître.
fr.B: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur ordonnait sévèrement de ne pas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire connaître.
fr.R: Mais Jésus leur a ordonné avec force de ne pas dire aux gens qui {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} était.

sw.L: Naye alikuwa akiwakemea sana ili wasimfanye ajulikane.
sw.B: Lakini aliwaamuru kwa ukali wasimfanye ajulikane.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu aliwaonya vikali wasiwaambie watu {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ni nani.

decisions.choice: not to make him known: Jesus will not be proclaimed by demons
alternatives: he wanted to stay hidden forever
decisions.reason: As in 1:25 and 1:34, Jesus silences the spirits. Who he is must be learned in his own way, through his words, works and cross.

decisions.choice: rebuke: give a stern command
decisions.reason: The same word as in 1:25.

decisions.choice: ordenaba severamente (B); advertía con firmeza (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is a stern command here (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "reprendía".

decisions.choice: akiwakemea (rebuking them)
decisions.reason: "Kukemea" is a stern command or rebuke (m2), the same verb Literal uses when Jesus rebukes the wind (4:39); Balanced and Readable say "aliwaamuru kwa ukali" and "aliwaonya vikali" (ordered, warned sternly).

source.text: Καὶ ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος καὶ προσκαλεῖται οὓς ἤθελεν αὐτός, καὶ ἀπῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And he goes up onto the mountain and calls to [him] those whom he wanted himself, and they went to him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} goes up onto the mountain and calls to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] those whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} himself wanted, and they came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up into the hills and called to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the ones {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted, and they came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then Jesus went up on a mountain. He called the people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wanted to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they came.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 산으로 올라가신다. 그리고 그분 자신이 원하시는 사람들을 부르신다. 그러자 그들이 그분께 나아왔다.
ko.B: 예수께서 산에 올라가셔서, 원하시는 사람들을 부르셨다. 그러자 그들이 예수께 나아왔다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 산에 올라가셨다. 그리고 예수께서 직접 고르신 사람들을 부르셨다. 그들이 예수께 왔다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi lên núi và gọi đến những người chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn, và họ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lên vùng đồi núi và gọi những người chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn đến với mình, và họ đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu lên một ngọn núi. Ngài gọi những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} muốn đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ đến.

es.L: Y sube al monte y llama [junto a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}] a los que {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} quería, y fueron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Después subió a la región montañosa y llamó a los que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quería, y ellos se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Después Jesús subió a un monte. Llamó a los que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quería que fueran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y ellos fueron.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monte sur la montagne et appelle à [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}] ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et ils vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} monta dans la montagne et appela à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait, et ils vinrent auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus est monté dans les collines. Il a appelé ceux qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} voulait, et ils sont venus auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Naye anapanda mlimani na kuwaita wale {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} aliowataka, nao wakaenda {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.B: Kisha alipanda vilimani, akawaita wale aliowataka, nao wakaja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alipanda mlimani. Aliwaita watu aliowataka waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, nao wakaja.

decisions.choice: those whom he himself wanted: his own choice
decisions.reason: "Himself" stresses that the choice is Jesus' alone.

decisions.choice: the mountain: a place of meeting with God
decisions.reason: Mark names no mountain. Moses went up the mountain and God formed the twelve tribes into a people there (Exodus 19; 24:4).

decisions.choice: the mountain: the hill country above the lake
decisions.reason: The phrase often means the hills rather than a single peak.

decisions.choice: the hills
decisions.reason: Balanced follows the meaning note on the hill country.

decisions.choice: "산" at every level
decisions.reason: Korean "산" covers hills as well as mountains, so Balanced does not need the English "hills" and keeps the link to the mountain as a place of meeting with God.

decisions.choice: la región montañosa
decisions.reason: As in English: the hill country above the lake (meaning decision m3). Literal and Readable keep "monte", which can carry the echo of meeting with God (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él mismo|Él mismo}} (L); {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The stressed pronoun shows it was Jesus's own choice (meaning decision m1); Spanish writes it, so it takes the span.

decisions.choice: la montagne (L, B); les collines (R)
decisions.reason: As in the French of John 6:3: "monter dans la montagne" is the usual French for going up into the hill country without naming a peak (meaning decision m3), so Balanced can keep the Greek word and its possible echo of meeting God on the mountain (m2). Readable gives the plain picture.

decisions.choice: ceux qu’il voulait, lui (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek adds "he himself" to stress his own choice (meaning decision m1). French marks that stress with the detached pronoun after the verb; "lui-même" there would read as an object.

source.text: καὶ ἐποίησεν δώδεκα, ἵνα ὦσιν μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν καὶ ἔχειν ἐξουσίαν ἐκβάλλειν τὰ δαιμόνια·

records.literal_gloss: And he made twelve, so that they might be with him and so that he might send them to proclaim \v 15 and to have authority to cast out the demons;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appointed twelve, so that they might be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} might send them out to proclaim \v 15 and to have authority to cast out the demons;
en.B: He appointed twelve to be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to be sent out to proclaim the message \v 15 with authority to throw out demons.
en.R: He chose twelve of them. He wanted them to stay with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and to go out and tell people the good news. \v 15 He would give them power to make demons leave people.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 열둘을 세우셨다. 그들이 그분과 함께 있게 하시고, 또 그들을 보내어 선포하게 하시고 \v 15 귀신들을 쫓아내는 권한을 가지게 하시려는 것이었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 열둘을 세우셨다. 그들을 자기와 함께 있게 하시고, 또 내보내어 말씀을 전하게 하시며, \v 15 귀신을 쫓아내는 권한을 가지게 하시려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 그 사람들 가운데 열두 명을 뽑으셨다. 그들이 예수와 함께 지내게 하시려는 것이었다. 또 그들을 보내서 사람들에게 기쁜 소식을 전하게 하시려는 것이었다. \v 15 예수께서는 그들에게 귀신을 사람들에게서 쫓아낼 수 있는 권한도 주시려고 하셨다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lập mười hai [người], để họ ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và để {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sai họ đi rao giảng \v 15 và có thẩm quyền đuổi các quỷ;
vi.B: Ngài lập mười hai người để ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và để được sai đi rao giảng, \v 15 với thẩm quyền đuổi quỷ.
vi.R: Ngài chọn mười hai người trong số họ. Ngài muốn họ ở với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và đi ra rao truyền Tin Lành cho mọi người. \v 15 Ngài sẽ ban cho họ quyền đuổi quỷ ra khỏi người ta.

es.L: Y constituyó a doce, para que estuvieran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y para enviarlos a proclamar \v 15 y a tener autoridad para expulsar los demonios;
es.B: Designó a doce para que estuvieran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y para enviarlos a anunciar el mensaje, \v 15 con autoridad para expulsar demonios.
es.R: Escogió a doce de ellos. Quería que se quedaran con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y que salieran a anunciar la buena noticia a la gente. \v 15 Les daría poder para obligar a los demonios a salir de las personas.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [en] établit douze, pour qu’ils soient avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et pour les envoyer proclamer \v 15 et avoir autorité pour chasser les démons ;
fr.B: Il en établit douze pour qu’ils soient avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et pour les envoyer proclamer le message, \v 15 avec autorité pour chasser les démons.
fr.R: Il en a choisi douze. Il voulait qu’ils restent avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et qu’ils partent annoncer la bonne nouvelle aux gens. \v 15 Il allait leur donner le pouvoir de chasser les démons.

sw.L: Naye akawaweka kumi na wawili, ili wawe pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} na ili awatume kuhubiri \v 15 na kuwa na mamlaka ya kutoa pepo;
sw.B: Aliwaweka kumi na wawili ili wawe pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, na ili awatume kuhubiri ujumbe \v 15 wakiwa na mamlaka ya kufukuza pepo.
sw.R: Aliwachagua kumi na wawili kati yao. Alitaka wakae pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}}, na awatume kwenda kuwaambia watu Habari Njema. \v 15 Angewapa uwezo wa kuwafanya pepo watoke ndani ya watu.

decisions.choice: made: appointed, set up
decisions.reason: The verb is used for appointing to an office, as Samuel says God "made" Moses and Aaron (1 Samuel 12:6).

decisions.choice: twelve: the number of Israel's tribes
alternatives: only the size of the group
decisions.reason: Twelve men stand for a renewed Israel gathered around Jesus.

decisions.choice: to be with him: the first purpose, before the sending
decisions.reason: They are to learn by living with him, then to be sent out (6:7) to preach and cast out demons, as he does (1:39).

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has twelve, without "whom he also named apostles"
alternatives: add: whom he also named apostles
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts add these words after "twelve", likely from Luke 6:13. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: throw out (B); make demons leave people (R)
decisions.reason: The same words as at 1:34.

decisions.choice: "귀신" for daimonion, "쫓아내다" for cast out, "권한" for authority
decisions.reason: "귀신" is the word of the Korean John (8:48; 10:20) and keeps "마귀" for the devil; "권한" is authority given by someone, as at John 1:12. Kept through the book.

decisions.choice: "mười hai [người]"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese needs a noun after a number, so Literal brackets "người".

decisions.choice: "đuổi quỷ" for casting out demons (whole book)
decisions.reason: "Quỷ" is the word the Vietnamese John uses for demons ("bị quỷ ám", 7:20; 10:20). "Đuổi" keeps the picture of driving out; "trừ tà" belongs to folk exorcism.

decisions.choice: constituyó (L); designó (B); escogió (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "made" means appointed (meaning decision m1). "Constituir" is both "make" and "set up"; Balanced and Readable use the plain words.

decisions.choice: expulsar (L, B); obligar a salir (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:34: the verb for driving out with force, used for demons throughout Mark; Readable says it in plain words.

decisions.choice: chasser les démons at every level
decisions.reason: "Chasser" is the plain French verb for driving demons out, so Readable needs no paraphrase where the English Readable has one.

decisions.choice: kutoa pepo (L); kufukuza pepo (B); kuwafanya pepo watoke (R)
decisions.reason: "Pepo" is the word for demons, as in John 8:48. "Kutoa pepo" is the usual phrase for casting them out; Balanced says "kufukuza" (drive out), which carries the force of the Greek verb, and Readable "make demons come out of people", as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐποίησεν τοὺς δώδεκα, καὶ ἐπέθηκεν ὄνομα τῷ Σίμωνι Πέτρον, καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ζεβεδαίου καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Ἰακώβου καὶ ἐπέθηκεν αὐτοῖς ὀνόματα Βοανηργές, ὅ ἐστιν Υἱοὶ Βροντῆς, καὶ Ἀνδρέαν καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν καὶ Ἰάκωβον τὸν τοῦ Ἁλφαίου καὶ Θαδδαῖον καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν Καναναῖον καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰσκαριώθ, ὃς καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And he made the twelve, and he put on name to the Simon Peter, \v 17 and James the [son] of the Zebedee and John the brother of the James, and he put on them name[s] Boanerges, which is, Sons of thunder, \v 18 and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James the [son] of the Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean \v 19 and Judas Iscariot, who also handed over him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appointed the twelve: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave Simon the name Peter, \v 17 and James the [son] of Zebedee and John the brother of James, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them the name Boanerges, which is "Sons of Thunder," \v 18 and Andrew and Philip and Bartholomew and Matthew and Thomas and James the [son] of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean \v 19 and Judas Iscariot, who also handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appointed the twelve. To Simon {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the name Peter. \v 17 James son of Zebedee and John, James's brother, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called Boanerges, that is, "Sons of Thunder." \v 18 Then there were Andrew and Philip, Bartholomew and Matthew, Thomas and James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus and Simon the Cananaean, \v 19 and Judas Iscariot, who went on to betray {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: These are the twelve men Jesus chose. He gave Simon a new name, Peter. \v 17 There were James and his brother John, the sons of Zebedee. Jesus gave them the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder." \v 18 There were also Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, and Simon, who was called the Zealot. \v 19 The last was Judas Iscariot. He was the one who later turned Jesus over to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 열둘을 세우셨는데, 시몬에게 베드로라는 이름을 붙이시고, \v 17 세베대의 [아들] 야고보와 야고보의 형제 요한에게는 보아너게, 곧 "천둥의 아들들"이라는 이름을 붙이셨으며, \v 18 또 안드레와 빌립과 바돌로매와 마태와 도마와 알패오의 [아들] 야고보와 다대오와 가나나인 시몬과 \v 19 가룟 유다를 [세우셨다]. 이 유다가 그분을 넘겨준 사람이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 열둘을 세우셨다. 시몬에게는 베드로라는 이름을 지어 주셨다. \v 17 세베대의 아들 야고보와 그의 형제 요한에게는 보아너게, 곧 "천둥의 아들들"이라는 이름을 지어 주셨다. \v 18 그리고 안드레, 빌립, 바돌로매, 마태, 도마, 알패오의 아들 야고보, 다대오, 가나나인 시몬, \v 19 그리고 가룟 유다가 있었다. 유다는 나중에 예수를 배반한 사람이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 뽑으신 열두 사람은 이렇다. 예수께서는 시몬에게 베드로라는 새 이름을 주셨다. \v 17 세베대의 아들 야고보와 그의 형제 요한도 있었다. 예수께서는 이 두 사람에게 보아너게라는 이름을 주셨는데, "천둥의 아들들"이라는 뜻이다. \v 18 또 안드레, 빌립, 바돌로매, 마태, 도마, 알패오의 아들 야고보, 다대오, 그리고 열심당원이라고 불리던 시몬도 있었다. \v 19 마지막은 가룟 유다였다. 그는 나중에 예수를 원수들에게 넘겨준 사람이다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lập mười hai [người]: và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tên cho Si-môn là Phi-e-rơ, \v 17 và Gia-cơ [con] của Xê-bê-đê và Giăng, anh em của Gia-cơ, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt cho họ tên là Bô-a-nẹt, nghĩa là "Con của Sấm Sét", \v 18 và Anh-rê và Phi-líp và Ba-thê-lê-my và Ma-thi-ơ và Thô-ma và Gia-cơ [con] của A-phê và Tha-đê và Si-môn người Ca-na-an \v 19 và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, là người cũng đã nộp {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Vậy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lập mười hai người. Ngài đặt cho Si-môn tên là Phi-e-rơ. \v 17 Gia-cơ con Xê-bê-đê và Giăng, anh em của Gia-cơ, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi là Bô-a-nẹt, nghĩa là "Con của Sấm Sét". \v 18 Rồi có Anh-rê và Phi-líp, Ba-thê-lê-my và Ma-thi-ơ, Thô-ma và Gia-cơ con A-phê, Tha-đê và Si-môn người Ca-na-an, \v 19 và Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt, người về sau đã phản bội {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Đây là mười hai người Đức Giê-xu đã chọn. Ngài đặt cho Si-môn một tên mới là Phi-e-rơ. \v 17 Có hai anh em Gia-cơ và Giăng, con của Xê-bê-đê. Đức Giê-xu đặt cho hai người tên là Bô-a-nẹt, nghĩa là "Con của Sấm Sét". \v 18 Còn có Anh-rê, Phi-líp, Ba-thê-lê-my, Ma-thi-ơ, Thô-ma, Gia-cơ con A-phê, Tha-đê, và Si-môn, người được gọi là "người Nhiệt Thành". \v 19 Người cuối cùng là Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt. Đó là người về sau đã nộp Đức Giê-xu cho kẻ thù của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

es.L: Y constituyó a los doce: y a Simón le puso por nombre Pedro, \v 17 y a Santiago el [hijo] de Zebedeo y a Juan el hermano de Santiago, y les puso por nombre Boanerges, que es «Hijos del Trueno», \v 18 y a Andrés y a Felipe y a Bartolomé y a Mateo y a Tomás y a Santiago el [hijo] de Alfeo y a Tadeo y a Simón el cananeo \v 19 y a Judas Iscariote, el que también {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregó.
es.B: Así designó a los doce. A Simón le dio el nombre de Pedro. \v 17 A Santiago, hijo de Zebedeo, y a Juan, hermano de Santiago, les puso por nombre Boanerges, es decir, «Hijos del Trueno». \v 18 Además estaban Andrés y Felipe, Bartolomé y Mateo, Tomás y Santiago, hijo de Alfeo, Tadeo y Simón el cananeo, \v 19 y Judas Iscariote, el que después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} traicionó.
es.R: Estos son los doce hombres que Jesús escogió. A Simón le dio un nombre nuevo: Pedro. \v 17 Estaban Santiago y su hermano Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo. Jesús les dio el nombre de Boanerges, que significa «Hijos del Trueno». \v 18 También estaban Andrés, Felipe, Bartolomé, Mateo, Tomás, Santiago hijo de Alfeo, Tadeo y Simón, al que llamaban el Zelote. \v 19 El último era Judas Iscariote. Él fue quien más tarde entregó a Jesús a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} enemigos.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} établit les douze : et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna à Simon le nom de Pierre, \v 17 et Jacques, le [fils] de Zébédée, et Jean, le frère de Jacques, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur donna le nom de Boanergès, c’est-à-dire « Fils du tonnerre », \v 18 et André, et Philippe, et Barthélemy, et Matthieu, et Thomas, et Jacques, le [fils] d’Alphée, et Thaddée, et Simon le Cananéen, \v 19 et Judas Iscariot, qui aussi {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} livra.
fr.B: Il établit donc les Douze. À Simon, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donna le nom de Pierre. \v 17 Jacques, fils de Zébédée, et Jean, frère de Jacques, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les appela Boanergès, c’est-à-dire « Fils du tonnerre ». \v 18 Il y avait aussi André et Philippe, Barthélemy et Matthieu, Thomas et Jacques fils d’Alphée, Thaddée et Simon le Cananéen, \v 19 et Judas Iscariot, celui qui allait {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} trahir.
fr.R: Voici les douze hommes que Jésus a choisis. Il a donné à Simon un nouveau nom : Pierre. \v 17 Il y avait Jacques et son frère Jean, les fils de Zébédée. Jésus leur a donné le nom de Boanergès, ce qui veut dire « Fils du tonnerre ». \v 18 Il y avait aussi André, Philippe, Barthélemy, Matthieu, Thomas, Jacques fils d’Alphée, Thaddée, et Simon, qu’on appelait le Zélote. \v 19 Le dernier était Judas Iscariot. C’est lui qui, plus tard, a livré Jésus à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} ennemis.

sw.L: Naye akawaweka wale kumi na wawili: akampa Simoni jina Petro, \v 17 na Yakobo [mwana] wa Zebedayo na Yohana ndugu wa Yakobo, akawapa jina Boanerge, yaani, "Wana wa Ngurumo," \v 18 na Andrea na Filipo na Bartholomayo na Mathayo na Tomaso na Yakobo [mwana] wa Alfayo na Thadayo na Simoni Mkananayo \v 19 na Yuda Iskariote, ambaye pia alimsaliti.
sw.B: Basi akawaweka wale kumi na wawili. Simoni alimpa jina Petro. \v 17 Yakobo mwana wa Zebedayo na Yohana, ndugu yake Yakobo, aliwaita Boanerge, yaani, "Wana wa Ngurumo." \v 18 Kisha kulikuwa na Andrea na Filipo, Bartholomayo na Mathayo, Tomaso na Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, Thadayo na Simoni Mkananayo, \v 19 na Yuda Iskariote, ambaye baadaye alimsaliti.
sw.R: Hawa ndio wale watu kumi na wawili ambao Yesu aliwachagua. Simoni alimpa jina jipya, Petro. \v 17 Walikuwepo Yakobo na ndugu yake Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo. Yesu aliwapa jina Boanerge, maana yake "Wana wa Ngurumo." \v 18 Walikuwepo pia Andrea, Filipo, Bartholomayo, Mathayo, Tomaso, Yakobo mwana wa Alfayo, Thadayo, na Simoni, aliyeitwa Mzelote. \v 19 Wa mwisho alikuwa Yuda Iskariote. Yeye ndiye ambaye baadaye alimtoa Yesu kwa adui {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

decisions.choice: and he appointed the twelve: the SBLGNT repeats the words of 3:14
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts do not repeat "he appointed the twelve". The repetition opens the list. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Peter: a rock
decisions.reason: Peter is the Greek for rock, like the Aramaic Cephas (John 1:42). From here on Mark calls Simon "Peter".

decisions.choice: Boanerges, Sons of Thunder: a Semitic nickname
alternatives: a title of honor in heaven
decisions.reason: Mark explains the Aramaic name. "Sons of" means men marked by something; it may fit their fiery temper (9:38; Luke 9:54).

decisions.choice: the Cananaean: from an Aramaic word for zeal, the Zealot
decisions.reason: Luke 6:15 calls him the Zealot. The name may mean he was zealous for the law, or belonged to those who wanted to throw off Roman rule.

decisions.choice: Iscariot: most likely "man from Kerioth", a town in Judea
decisions.reason: The meaning is not certain; the most common view is a place name.

decisions.choice: handed over: betrayed him to his enemies
