decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of John's arrest (1:14). Mark tells the betrayal in chapter 14.

decisions.choice: So he appointed the twelve (B); These are the twelve men Jesus chose (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the opening as a sentence of its own; Readable turns it into a heading for the list.

decisions.choice: who was called the Zealot
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name, as Luke does.

decisions.choice: betrayed (B); turned Jesus over to his enemies (R)
decisions.reason: In this sentence the word means betrayal, which Balanced and Readable name.

decisions.choice: "천둥의 아들들"
decisions.reason: "우레" is the older word of familiar versions; "천둥" is the everyday word for thunder today.

decisions.choice: Protestant name forms: "바돌로매", "다대오", "가나나인 시몬" (L, B), "열심당원" (R), "가룟 유다"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant forms (style guide, section 5). Readable gives the meaning of "Cananaean" (zealot) as the English Readable does, with the usual Korean word "열심당원".

decisions.choice: Bô-a-nẹt, Ba-thê-lê-my, Ma-thi-ơ, Tha-đê, A-phê, Xê-bê-đê
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliterations, as the style guide settles for names; Giăng, Phi-e-rơ, Anh-rê, Thô-ma and Giu-đa Ích-ca-ri-ốt as in the Vietnamese John.

decisions.choice: "anh em của Gia-cơ" (L, B); "hai anh em" (R)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese normally says whether a brother is older or younger; Mark does not, so "anh em" leaves it open, as the Vietnamese John does for Andrew (1:40).

decisions.choice: "Si-môn người Ca-na-an" (L, B); "người được gọi là 'người Nhiệt Thành'" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the traditional form of Mark's word. A Vietnamese reader may take "người Ca-na-an" for a Canaanite, which it is not (the meaning decision says it comes from the Aramaic for "zeal"), so Readable says "Nhiệt Thành" (zealous) instead, as the English Readable says "the Zealot". A reviewer may prefer to avoid "Ca-na-an" at Balanced too.

decisions.choice: Santiago
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish name for the apostles James, as the Spanish of Galatians already has. "Jacobo" is the older form.

decisions.choice: el cananeo (L, B); al que llamaban el Zelote (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable gives the meaning of the Aramaic nickname (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: «Hijos del Trueno», in guillemets
decisions.reason: The narrator quotes the meaning of the name; Spanish uses guillemets for a quotation in narration.

decisions.choice: the names in their usual French form: Jacques, Zébédée, Boanergès, Barthélemy, Matthieu, Alphée, Thaddée, Simon le Cananéen (L, B) / le Zélote (R), Judas Iscariot
decisions.reason: The usual French spellings. "Cananéen" transcribes the Greek word (meaning decision m4); Readable says what it means, "le Zélote", as the English Readable does. "Fils du tonnerre" is the same in the singular and the plural in French.

decisions.choice: les douze (L); les Douze (B); les douze hommes (R)
decisions.reason: As in John 20:24, Balanced writes "les Douze" with a capital when the number names the group; Literal keeps the bare number as the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: le livra (L); allait le trahir (B); a livré Jésus à ses ennemis (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to hand over, here to his enemies (meaning decision m6). Literal keeps "livrer", Balanced says "trahir" as the English says "betray", and Readable spells out to whom.

decisions.choice: Yakobo, Zebedayo, Bartholomayo, Mathayo, Alfayo, Thadayo, Mkananayo (L, B), Mzelote (R), Yuda Iskariote
decisions.reason: The names in their usual Swahili forms, with Yakobo, Zebedayo, Tomaso and Yuda Iskariote as in John. "Mkananayo" keeps the Greek title; Readable says "Mzelote" (the Zealot), what the title means (m4), as the English Readable does. "Wana wa Ngurumo" translates "Sons of Thunder".

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχεται εἰς οἶκον· καὶ συνέρχεται πάλιν ὁ ὄχλος, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι αὐτοὺς μηδὲ ἄρτον φαγεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And he comes into a house; and comes together again the crowd, so that not to be able them not even bread to eat.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes home; and the crowd gathers again, so that they were not even able to eat bread.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went home, and again such a crowd gathered that they could not even eat a meal.
en.R: Then Jesus went into a house. Once again a crowd came together. So many people came that Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} followers did not even have time to eat.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 집으로 들어가신다. 그러자 무리가 다시 모여든다. 그래서 그들은 빵을 먹을 수조차 없었다.
ko.B: 예수께서 집에 돌아오시자, 다시 무리가 모여들어서 그들은 음식을 먹을 겨를조차 없었다.
ko.R: 그 뒤에 예수께서 어떤 집에 들어가셨다. 그러자 또 사람들이 많이 모여들었다. 사람들이 너무 많아서 예수와 제자들은 밥 먹을 시간도 없었다.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về nhà; và đám đông lại tụ họp, đến nỗi họ thậm chí không thể ăn bánh được.
vi.B: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về nhà, và đám đông lại kéo đến, đến nỗi thầy trò không có cả thì giờ để ăn.
vi.R: Sau đó Đức Giê-xu vào một ngôi nhà. Đám đông lại kéo đến. Người ta đến đông quá, đến nỗi Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ không có cả thì giờ để ăn.

es.L: Y viene a casa; y se reúne otra vez la multitud, de modo que ellos ni siquiera podían comer pan.
es.B: Luego volvió a casa, y otra vez se juntó tanta gente que ni siquiera podían comer.
es.R: Después Jesús entró en una casa. Otra vez se reunió una multitud. Había tanta gente que Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos ni siquiera tenían tiempo para comer.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vient à la maison ; et la foule s’assemble de nouveau, de sorte qu’ils ne pouvaient même pas manger de pain.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rentra à la maison, et la foule s’y rassembla de nouveau, si bien qu’ils ne pouvaient même pas prendre leur repas.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus est entré dans une maison. De nouveau, beaucoup de gens se sont rassemblés. Il y avait tellement de monde que Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples n’avaient même pas le temps de manger.

sw.L: Naye anakuja nyumbani; na umati unakusanyika tena, hata wao wasiweze hata kula mkate.
sw.B: Kisha akaenda nyumbani, na tena umati mkubwa ukakusanyika, hata wao hawakuweza hata kula chakula.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu aliingia katika nyumba moja. Umati wa watu ukakusanyika tena. Watu walikuwa wengi sana hata Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} hawakupata hata nafasi ya kula.

decisions.choice: into a house: home, most likely in Capernaum
decisions.reason: The phrase is the same as in 2:1, "at home".

decisions.choice: eat bread: eat a meal
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general.

decisions.choice: they: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: The ones who cannot eat are Jesus and those with him.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his followers
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are.

decisions.choice: "빵을 먹다" (L); "음식을 먹다" (B); "밥 먹다" (R)
decisions.reason: "Eat bread" means eat a meal (meaning decision). Literal keeps "빵" (never "떡", style guide section 6); Balanced and Readable use the Korean words for a meal.

decisions.choice: "thầy trò" for "they"
decisions.reason: "Họ" after the crowd would point to the crowd; "thầy trò" (teacher and disciples) is the natural Vietnamese way to say Jesus and his disciples together.

decisions.choice: Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names who "they" are (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: kula mkate (L); kula chakula (B); kula (R)
decisions.reason: "Eat bread" means eat a meal (m2). Literal keeps "mkate"; Balanced says "chakula" (food, a meal), since "kula mkate" in Swahili means eating bread and nothing else.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ παρ’ αὐτοῦ ἐξῆλθον κρατῆσαι αὐτόν, ἔλεγον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξέστη.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard, those from him went out to seize him; they were saying for that He is out of [his] mind.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people heard, they went out to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for they were saying, "He is out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind."
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} family heard about this, they set out to take charge of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because they were saying, "He has lost {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} senses."
en.R: Jesus' family heard about this. They went to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} home by force, because they said, "He has gone crazy."

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 집안 사람들이 듣고 그분을 붙잡으러 나섰다. 그들이 "그가 정신이 나갔다" 하고 말하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수의 가족이 이 소식을 듣고 예수를 붙들어 오려고 나섰다. 그들이 "그가 제정신이 아니다" 하고 말하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 예수의 가족이 이 소식을 들었다. 그들은 예수를 억지로 집으로 데려가려고 나섰다. 그들이 "그가 미쳤다!" 하고 말했기 때문이다.

vi.L: Và khi người nhà của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe [vậy], họ đi ra để bắt giữ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì họ nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã mất trí.
vi.B: Khi người nhà của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nghe tin ấy, họ ra đi để đem {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về, vì họ nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã mất trí.
vi.R: Gia đình của Đức Giê-xu nghe tin ấy. Họ đi đến để bắt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về nhà, vì họ nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mất trí rồi.

es.L: Y al oír[lo] los {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}}, salieron para apoderarse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque decían: «Está fuera de {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}».
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} familia se enteró, salieron a hacerse cargo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque decían: «Ha perdido el juicio».
es.R: La familia de Jesús se enteró de esto. Fueron a llevárselo a casa a la fuerza, porque decían: «Se ha vuelto loco».

fr.L: Et, ayant entendu, ceux de chez {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} sortirent pour se saisir de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, car ils disaient : « Il a perdu la raison. »
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} proches apprirent cela, ils partirent pour se saisir de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, car ils disaient : « Il a perdu la raison. »
fr.R: La famille de Jésus a appris ce qui se passait. Ses proches sont venus pour {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ramener de force à la maison, parce qu’ils disaient : « Il est devenu fou. »

sw.L: Na watu wa {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} waliposikia, walitoka ili wamkamate, kwa maana walikuwa wakisema, "Amerukwa na akili."
sw.B: Watu wa familia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} waliposikia habari hizi, walitoka kwenda kumchukua kwa nguvu, kwa sababu walikuwa wakisema, "Amerukwa na akili."
sw.R: Familia ya Yesu ilisikia habari hizi. Wakaenda kumchukua na kumrudisha nyumbani kwa nguvu, kwa sababu walisema, "Amechanganyikiwa!"

decisions.choice: those from him: his family, who come in 3:31
decisions.reason: The phrase means those close to someone, usually his relatives. Mark tells of his mother and brothers arriving in 3:31.

decisions.choice: seize: take hold of by force
decisions.reason: The verb is used for arrest (6:17; 14:1). His family want to take him away for his own good.

decisions.choice: they were saying: his family, or people in general
decisions.reason: "They" is most likely the family. It could be people in general, whose talk the family heard.

decisions.choice: out of his mind: beside himself
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand outside oneself. Here it means mad, as the scribes' charge in 3:22 shows.

decisions.choice: take him home by force
decisions.reason: Readable says what the family meant to do.

decisions.choice: "그가" with no honorific in the quoted words
decisions.reason: The speakers think he has lost his mind; giving him honorifics in their mouths would misrepresent what they say. The narrator still honours him.

decisions.choice: indirect speech: "họ nói rằng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã mất trí"
alternatives: a direct quotation ("Anh ấy mất trí rồi")
decisions.reason: A direct quotation would force Vietnamese to say who speaks and how they address Jesus (his mother, his brothers, or people in general), which the Greek leaves open. Reported speech keeps "họ" as open as the meaning decision does; the Greek "hoti" allows either reading.

decisions.choice: los {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}} (L); {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} familia (B); la familia de Jesús (R)
decisions.reason: "Los suyos" keeps the Greek "those from him" open in Literal; Balanced and Readable follow the meaning decision that these are his family.

decisions.choice: Il a perdu la raison (L, B); Il est devenu fou (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be beside oneself, out of one’s mind (meaning decision m4). French "être hors de soi" now means to be furious, which would change the charge, so every level says plainly that they thought he had lost his mind.

decisions.choice: ceux de chez lui (L); ses proches (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek "those from him" means his family (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the vague expression, Balanced says "ses proches". "Ils disaient" keeps it open whether his family or people in general were saying it (m3).

decisions.choice: amerukwa na akili (L, B); amechanganyikiwa (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek says he is "out of himself", beside himself (m4). "Amerukwa na akili" is the phrase John 10:20 uses for the same charge; Readable uses the everyday "amechanganyikiwa" (he has gone crazy).

source.text: καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβάντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Βεελζεβοὺλ ἔχει καὶ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ἄρχοντι τῶν δαιμονίων ἐκβάλλει τὰ δαιμόνια.

records.literal_gloss: And the scribes those from Jerusalem having come down were saying, Beelzebul he has, and, By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.

en.L: And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying, "He has Beelzebul," and, "By the ruler of the demons {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} casts out the demons."
en.B: Scribes who had come down from Jerusalem claimed, "Beelzebul has hold of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!" and, "It is by the ruler of the demons that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} throws out demons!"
en.R: Some teachers of God's law had come from Jerusalem. They said, "Beelzebul, the ruler of demons, is living in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! That is how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} forces demons to leave people!"

ko.L: 그리고 예루살렘에서 내려온 율법학자들은 "그는 바알세불이 들렸다" 하고, 또 "그는 귀신들의 우두머리를 힘입어 귀신들을 쫓아낸다" 하고 말하고 있었다.
ko.B: 예루살렘에서 내려온 율법학자들은 "그는 바알세불에게 사로잡혔다!" 하고, "그는 귀신들의 우두머리의 힘을 빌려 귀신을 쫓아낸다!" 하고 말했다.
ko.R: 예루살렘에서 율법을 가르치는 선생들이 몇 사람 내려와 있었다. 그들이 말했다. "귀신들의 우두머리인 바알세불이 저 사람 속에 들어 있다! 그래서 저 사람이 귀신들을 쫓아낼 수 있는 것이다!"

vi.L: Và các thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem xuống thì nói: "Ông ta có Bê-ên-xê-bun," và: "Ông ta nhờ kẻ cai trị các quỷ mà đuổi các quỷ."
vi.B: Các thầy thông giáo từ Giê-ru-sa-lem xuống thì cho rằng: "Ông ta bị Bê-ên-xê-bun ám!" và: "Ông ta nhờ chúa quỷ mà đuổi quỷ!"
vi.R: Có mấy thầy dạy luật từ Giê-ru-sa-lem xuống. Họ nói: "Bê-ên-xê-bun, chúa của các quỷ, đang ở trong ông ta! Nhờ vậy ông ta mới đuổi được quỷ ra khỏi người ta!"

es.L: Y los escribas que habían bajado de Jerusalén decían: «Tiene a Beelzebul», y: «Por el príncipe de los demonios expulsa los demonios».
es.B: Unos escribas que habían bajado de Jerusalén afirmaban: «¡Beelzebul se ha apoderado de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!», y: «¡Expulsa a los demonios por el poder del príncipe de los demonios!».
es.R: Algunos maestros de la ley de Dios habían venido de Jerusalén. Decían: «¡Beelzebul, el jefe de los demonios, vive dentro de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}! ¡Por eso puede obligar a los demonios a salir de la gente!».

fr.L: Et les scribes qui étaient descendus de Jérusalem disaient : « Il a Béelzébul », et : « C’est par le chef des démons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} chasse les démons. »
fr.B: Des scribes descendus de Jérusalem affirmaient : « Il est possédé par Béelzébul ! » et : « C’est par le chef des démons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} chasse les démons ! »
fr.R: Il y avait là des spécialistes de la Loi de Dieu venus de Jérusalem. Ils disaient : « Béelzébul, le chef des démons, est en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ! C’est comme cela qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} oblige les démons à sortir des gens ! »

sw.L: Na waandishi waliokuwa wameshuka kutoka Yerusalemu walikuwa wakisema, "Ana Beelzebuli," na, "Kwa mkuu wa pepo anatoa pepo."
sw.B: Waandishi waliokuwa wameshuka kutoka Yerusalemu walidai, "Amepagawa na Beelzebuli!" na, "Ni kwa nguvu za mkuu wa pepo anafukuza pepo!"
sw.R: Walimu wa Sheria walikuwa wamekuja kutoka Yerusalemu. Walisema, "Beelzebuli, mkuu wa pepo, anakaa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}! Ndiyo sababu anaweza kuwafukuza pepo watoke ndani ya watu!"

decisions.choice: Beelzebul: a name for the prince of demons, Satan (3:23)
decisions.reason: The name may come from Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron (2 Kings 1:2), or mean "lord of the house" (compare 3:27). Here it names Satan.

decisions.choice: he has Beelzebul: he is possessed by Beelzebul
alternatives: he works with Beelzebul as a partner
decisions.reason: "Has" is used for being possessed by a spirit, as in 3:30.

decisions.choice: scribes from Jerusalem: official teachers from the capital
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was the center of religious authority. Their coming down shows that Jesus is now watched from the capital.

decisions.choice: two charges: he is possessed, and he casts out demons by Satan's power
decisions.reason: The Greek gives two sayings, each introduced. Jesus answers both (3:23-30).

decisions.choice: Beelzebul, the ruler of demons, is living in him
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two charges and says who Beelzebul is.

decisions.choice: "율법학자" (L, B); "율법을 가르치는 선생" (R) for the scribes
decisions.reason: "율법학자" is the word of the Korean John (8:3) and says what these men were; "서기관" (clerk) is the older church word and misleads today. Readable describes their work.

decisions.choice: "바알세불이 들렸다"; the scribes speak of Jesus as "그" / "저 사람" with no honorific
decisions.reason: "He has Beelzebul" means he is possessed (meaning decision), which Korean says with "들리다" as of a demon; the speakers are hostile, so their words give him no honorific, as in John 11:48.

decisions.choice: thầy thông giáo (L, B); thầy dạy luật (R) for the scribes (whole book)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese John (8:3): "thầy thông giáo" is the established Protestant term, "kinh sư" the Catholic one; Readable says what they did.

decisions.choice: "ông ta" for Jesus in his accusers' words, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The style guide: opponents speak of him as "ông ta". Where the English has "him" under the setting, Vietnamese has a word with no reverent capital.

decisions.choice: Bê-ên-xê-bun
decisions.reason: The Protestant transliteration of the name.

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:22: Readable says what the scribes were.

decisions.choice: Beelzebul
decisions.reason: The form of the SBLGNT, as in English. "Beelzebú" is the form most Spanish readers know.

decisions.choice: Béelzébul
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT spelling (Beelzebul, meaning decision m1) in its usual French form.

decisions.choice: les scribes (L, B); des spécialistes de la Loi de Dieu (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: "Scribes" is the term used in John 8:3; for new readers it suggests only copyists, so Readable says what they were, teachers expert in God’s Law, as the English Readable does (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa Sheria (R)
alternatives: walimu wa sheria at every level
decisions.reason: As in John 8:3: "waandishi" (writers) is the established Swahili name for the scribes; Readable says what they did, "walimu wa Sheria" (teachers of the Law). For the whole book.

decisions.choice: Amepagawa na Beelzebuli (Beelzebul has possessed him)
decisions.reason: "He has Beelzebul" means he is possessed by him (m2). Literal keeps "Ana Beelzebuli"; Balanced uses "kupagawa", the Swahili word for being possessed by a spirit. The name is given the Swahili ending, "Beelzebuli".

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Πῶς δύναται Σατανᾶς Σατανᾶν ἐκβάλλειν;

records.literal_gloss: And having called them to [him], in parables he was saying to them, How is able Satan Satan to cast out?

en.L: And calling them to [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying to them in parables, "How can Satan cast out Satan?
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called them over and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan throw out Satan?
en.R: So Jesus called them to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He used word pictures to teach them. He said, "Satan cannot force himself out of people!

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들을 불러 비유로 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "사탄이 어떻게 사탄을 쫓아낼 수 있느냐?
ko.B: 그래서 예수께서 그들을 불러 놓고 비유로 말씀하셨다. "사탄이 어떻게 사탄을 쫓아낼 수 있겠느냐?
ko.R: 그래서 예수께서 그 사람들을 가까이 부르셨다. 그리고 비유, 곧 무엇에 빗대어 하는 이야기로 그들을 가르치셨다. 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "사탄이 사탄을 쫓아낼 수는 없다!

vi.L: Và sau khi gọi họ đến, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dùng các ngụ ngôn mà nói với họ: "Làm sao Sa-tan có thể đuổi Sa-tan?
vi.B: Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gọi họ lại và dùng ngụ ngôn nói với họ: "Làm sao Sa-tan đuổi Sa-tan được?
vi.R: Vì vậy, Đức Giê-xu gọi họ đến gần. Ngài dùng những hình ảnh so sánh để dạy họ. Ngài nói: "Sa-tan không thể tự đuổi chính mình ra khỏi người ta!

es.L: Y llamándolos [junto a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}}], les decía en parábolas: «¿Cómo puede Satanás expulsar a Satanás?
es.B: Entonces los llamó y les habló en parábolas: «¿Cómo puede Satanás expulsar a Satanás?
es.R: Entonces Jesús los llamó para que se acercaran. Les enseñó por medio de comparaciones. Les dijo: «¡Satanás no puede expulsarse a sí mismo de la gente!

fr.L: Et, les ayant appelés à [{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}], {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait en paraboles : « Comment Satan peut-il chasser Satan ?
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les fit venir et leur parla en paraboles : « Comment Satan pourrait-il chasser Satan ?
fr.R: Alors Jésus les a appelés près de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il leur a parlé avec des comparaisons. Il leur a dit : « Satan ne peut pas se chasser lui-même !

sw.L: Naye akawaita [{{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}], akawa akiwaambia kwa mifano, "Shetani awezaje kumtoa Shetani?
sw.B: Basi akawaita, akasema nao kwa mifano: "Shetani anawezaje kumfukuza Shetani?
sw.R: Basi Yesu aliwaita waje {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Akatumia mifano kuwafundisha. Akasema, "Shetani hawezi kujifukuza mwenyewe kutoka ndani ya watu!

decisions.choice: parables: picture sayings and short stories that make a comparison
decisions.reason: A parable can be a single image, like a divided kingdom or a strong man's house. Mark's first use of the word is here; chapter 4 is made of parables.

decisions.choice: how can Satan cast out Satan? a question that shows the charge makes no sense
decisions.reason: If Satan drove out his own demons, he would be fighting himself.

decisions.choice: word pictures
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a parable is.

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the question expects.

decisions.choice: "비유" at every level; Readable explains it once ("무엇에 빗대어 하는 이야기")
decisions.reason: "비유" is the established Korean word and is used in the Korean John (10:6; 16:25); it is common enough for Readable once it has been explained, so the parable chapter (Mark 4) can keep it.

decisions.choice: "ngụ ngôn" (L, B); "hình ảnh so sánh" (R) for parables (whole book; Readable says "câu chuyện" where a story is told, chapter 4)
decisions.reason: "Ngụ ngôn" is the usual modern word for Jesus' parables; "ví dụ" (the 1926 word) now means "example", and "ẩn dụ" is a grammar term. The Vietnamese John uses "lời ví von" for a different Greek word (paroimia, 10:6). Here the parables are short picture sayings, so Readable says "hình ảnh so sánh".

decisions.choice: comparaciones
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what a parable is; the sayings that follow are comparisons rather than stories.

decisions.choice: paraboles (L, B); des comparaisons (R)
decisions.reason: "Parabole" is the French word for these picture sayings (meaning decision m1). Readable says "comparaisons", since here the parables are short sayings, not stories; in chapter 4 Readable says "histoires".

decisions.choice: mifano (parables) at every level
decisions.reason: "Mfano" is a comparison, a saying or story that likens one thing to another (m1); it is the word John 16:25 uses for figures of speech, and it is plain enough for Readable. For the whole book.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν βασιλεία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δύναται σταθῆναι ἡ βασιλεία ἐκείνη·

records.literal_gloss: And if a kingdom against itself is divided, not is able to stand the kingdom that;

en.L: And if a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand;
en.B: If a kingdom splits into sides that fight each other, it cannot last.
en.R: If the people of a kingdom fight against each other, that kingdom will fall apart.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 한 나라가 자기 자신을 거슬러 갈라지면, 그 나라는 설 수 없다.
ko.B: 한 나라가 갈라져서 서로 싸우면, 그 나라는 버틸 수 없다.
ko.R: 한 나라의 백성이 서로 편을 갈라 싸우면, 그 나라는 무너지고 만다.

vi.L: Và nếu một vương quốc tự chia rẽ chống lại chính mình, vương quốc ấy không thể đứng vững;
vi.B: Nếu một vương quốc chia thành phe phái chống nhau, vương quốc ấy không thể tồn tại.
vi.R: Nếu dân trong một vương quốc đánh lẫn nhau, vương quốc ấy sẽ tan rã.

es.L: Y si un reino está dividido contra sí mismo, ese reino no puede mantenerse en pie;
es.B: Si un reino se divide en bandos que luchan entre sí, no puede durar.
es.R: Si la gente de un reino pelea entre sí, ese reino se derrumba.

fr.L: Et si un royaume est divisé contre lui-même, ce royaume-là ne peut pas tenir ;
fr.B: Si un royaume se divise en camps qui se combattent, il ne peut pas durer.
fr.R: Si les habitants d’un royaume se battent entre eux, ce royaume va s’écrouler.

sw.L: Na ufalme ukigawanyika dhidi yake wenyewe, ufalme huo hauwezi kusimama;
sw.B: Ufalme ukigawanyika makundi yanayopigana wenyewe kwa wenyewe, hauwezi kudumu.
sw.R: Watu wa ufalme mmoja wakipigana wenyewe kwa wenyewe, ufalme huo utaanguka.

decisions.choice: if a kingdom is divided: a general truth
alternatives: a real kingdom Jesus has in mind
decisions.reason: The saying states what is always true, as a proverb does.

decisions.choice: stand: hold firm, survive
decisions.reason: To stand is to last and not fall.

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν οἰκία ἐφ’ ἑαυτὴν μερισθῇ, οὐ δυνήσεται ἡ οἰκία ἐκείνη σταθῆναι·

records.literal_gloss: and if a house against itself is divided, not will be able the house that to stand.

en.L: and if a house is divided against itself, that house will not be able to stand.
en.B: If a household turns against itself, it will not hold together.
en.R: If the people in a family fight against each other, that family will not last.

ko.L: 또 만일 한 집이 자기 자신을 거슬러 갈라지면, 그 집은 설 수 없을 것이다.
ko.B: 한 집안이 갈라져서 서로 맞서면, 그 집안은 버티지 못할 것이다.
ko.R: 한 가족이 서로 싸우면, 그 가족은 오래가지 못한다.

vi.L: và nếu một nhà tự chia rẽ chống lại chính mình, nhà ấy sẽ không thể đứng vững.
vi.B: Nếu một gia đình chống lại chính mình, gia đình ấy sẽ không đứng vững.
vi.R: Nếu người trong một gia đình chống đối nhau, gia đình ấy sẽ không bền lâu.

es.L: y si una casa está dividida contra sí misma, esa casa no podrá mantenerse en pie.
es.B: Si una familia se pone en contra de sí misma, no podrá mantenerse unida.
es.R: Si los miembros de una familia pelean entre sí, esa familia no durará.

fr.L: et si une maison est divisée contre elle-même, cette maison-là ne pourra pas tenir.
fr.B: Si une famille se dresse contre elle-même, elle ne pourra pas rester unie.
fr.R: Si les membres d’une famille se battent entre eux, cette famille ne durera pas.

sw.L: na nyumba ikigawanyika dhidi yake yenyewe, nyumba hiyo haitaweza kusimama.
sw.B: Familia ikigawanyika na kupigana yenyewe kwa yenyewe, haitaweza kudumu.
sw.R: Watu wa familia moja wakipigana wenyewe kwa wenyewe, familia hiyo haitadumu.

decisions.choice: a house: a household, a family
decisions.reason: "House" means the people of a household, as often in the Bible.
The house is the household (meaning decision); Korean "집안" means the family as well as the building, so Balanced keeps both, and Readable says "가족".

decisions.choice: casa (L); familia (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a household (meaning decision m1). Spanish "casa" can mean that too, so Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: une maison (L); une famille (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means a household (meaning decision m1). French "maison" can say this but first suggests a building; Balanced and Readable say "famille".

decisions.choice: nyumba (L); familia (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek "house" here is a household, a family (m1). Literal keeps "nyumba", which can mean a household in Swahili too; Balanced and Readable say "familia" so that no reader thinks of a building.

source.text: καὶ εἰ ὁ Σατανᾶς ἀνέστη ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἐμερίσθη, οὐ δύναται στῆναι ἀλλὰ τέλος ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: And if the Satan rose up against himself and was divided, not he is able to stand but an end he has.

en.L: And if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but has an end.
en.B: So if Satan has rebelled against himself and is divided, he cannot last; his end has come.
en.R: So if Satan fights against himself, he will not last. That will be the end of him.

ko.L: 그리고 만일 사탄이 자기 자신을 거슬러 일어나 갈라졌다면, 그는 설 수 없고 끝이 난 것이다.
ko.B: 그러니 사탄이 자기 자신에게 맞서 일어나 갈라졌다면, 그는 버틸 수 없고 끝장이 난 것이다.
ko.R: 그러니 사탄이 자기 자신과 싸운다면, 사탄은 오래가지 못한다. 그것으로 사탄은 끝이다.

vi.L: Và nếu Sa-tan đã nổi lên chống lại chính mình và bị chia rẽ, nó không thể đứng vững, nhưng đã đến hồi kết thúc.
vi.B: Vậy nếu Sa-tan đã nổi lên chống lại chính mình và bị chia rẽ, nó không thể tồn tại; nó đã đến ngày tận số.
vi.R: Vậy nếu Sa-tan chống lại chính mình, nó sẽ không tồn tại được. Đó sẽ là ngày tận số của nó.

es.L: Y si Satanás se ha levantado contra sí mismo y está dividido, no puede mantenerse en pie, sino que tiene [su] fin.
es.B: Así que, si Satanás se ha rebelado contra sí mismo y está dividido, no puede durar; ha llegado su fin.
es.R: Así que, si Satanás pelea contra sí mismo, no durará. Ese será su fin.

fr.L: Et si Satan s’est dressé contre lui-même et s’est divisé, il ne peut pas tenir, mais il a une fin.
fr.B: Si donc Satan s’est révolté contre lui-même et qu’il est divisé, il ne peut pas durer : c’en est fini de lui.
fr.R: Si Satan se bat contre lui-même, il ne durera pas. Ce sera la fin pour lui.

sw.L: Na kama Shetani ameinuka dhidi yake mwenyewe na amegawanyika, hawezi kusimama, bali amefikia mwisho.
sw.B: Basi ikiwa Shetani ameasi dhidi yake mwenyewe na amegawanyika, hawezi kudumu; mwisho wake umefika.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Shetani akipigana na nafsi yake mwenyewe, hatadumu. Huo utakuwa mwisho wake.

decisions.choice: if Satan has risen up: an unreal case
alternatives: Jesus thinks Satan really is divided
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say Satan is divided. He shows where the scribes' charge would lead.

decisions.choice: has an end: is finished
decisions.reason: The phrase means he would be done for.

decisions.choice: Satan's rule is ending, but by another's power
decisions.reason: Satan is not falling by civil war. Jesus goes on to show that one stronger has come (3:27).

decisions.choice: "nó" for Satan
decisions.reason: "Nó" is the ordinary pronoun for a being one does not respect; the Vietnamese John uses only the name (13:27), and "hắn" would sound like a human villain.

source.text: ἀλλ’ οὐδεὶς δύναται εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν τοῦ ἰσχυροῦ εἰσελθὼν τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ διαρπάσαι ἐὰν μὴ πρῶτον τὸν ἰσχυρὸν δήσῃ, καὶ τότε τὴν οἰκίαν αὐτοῦ διαρπάσει.

records.literal_gloss: But no one is able into the house of the strong [man] having entered the goods of him to plunder, unless first the strong [man] he binds, and then the house of him he will plunder.

en.L: But no one can enter the strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
en.B: In fact, no one can break into a strong man's house and carry off his belongings without first tying him up. Only then can he rob the house.
en.R: No one can go into a strong man's house and steal his things unless he first ties up the strong man. After that he can take everything in the house.

ko.L: 그러나 아무도 먼저 그 힘센 사람을 묶지 않고서는, 힘센 사람의 집에 들어가 그의 세간을 털어 갈 수 없다. 묶은 뒤에야 그의 집을 털 것이다.
ko.B: 사실, 누구든지 힘센 사람의 집에 쳐들어가 그 살림살이를 빼앗아 가려면, 먼저 그 힘센 사람을 묶어야 한다. 그래야 그 집을 털 수 있다.
ko.R: 힘센 사람의 집에 들어가서 그 사람의 물건을 훔쳐 가려면, 먼저 그 힘센 사람을 꽁꽁 묶어야 한다. 그다음에야 그 집에 있는 것을 다 가져갈 수 있다.

vi.L: Nhưng không ai có thể vào nhà của người mạnh mà cướp đồ đạc của người ấy, nếu trước hết không trói người mạnh ấy lại; và rồi mới cướp nhà người ấy.
vi.B: Thật ra, không ai có thể xông vào nhà một người mạnh sức mà lấy đi đồ đạc của người ấy, nếu không trói người ấy lại trước. Chỉ khi đó mới cướp được nhà người ấy.
vi.R: Không ai có thể vào nhà một người rất khỏe mà lấy trộm đồ đạc của người ấy, nếu không trói người ấy lại trước. Sau đó mới lấy được mọi thứ trong nhà.

es.L: Pero nadie puede entrar en la casa del fuerte y saquear sus bienes si primero no ata al fuerte; y entonces saqueará su casa.
es.B: De hecho, nadie puede entrar en la casa de un hombre fuerte y llevarse sus pertenencias sin atarlo primero. Solo entonces podrá saquear la casa.
es.R: Nadie puede entrar en la casa de un hombre fuerte y robar sus cosas si antes no lo ata. Después de eso, puede llevarse todo lo que hay en la casa.

fr.L: Mais personne ne peut, étant entré dans la maison du [homme] fort, piller ses biens, s’il n’a d’abord lié le [homme] fort ; et alors il pillera sa maison.
fr.B: D’ailleurs, personne ne peut entrer dans la maison d’un homme fort et emporter ses biens sans l’avoir d’abord ligoté. Alors seulement il pourra piller sa maison.
fr.R: Personne ne peut entrer dans la maison d’un homme fort et voler ses affaires sans attacher d’abord cet homme. Après cela, il peut prendre tout ce qu’il y a dans la maison.

sw.L: Lakini hakuna mtu awezaye kuingia katika nyumba ya mwenye nguvu na kupora vitu vyake, asipomfunga kwanza yule mwenye nguvu; na hapo ndipo atakapoipora nyumba yake.
sw.B: Kwa kweli, hakuna mtu anayeweza kuvunja na kuingia katika nyumba ya mtu mwenye nguvu na kuchukua mali zake bila kumfunga kwanza. Hapo tu ndipo anaweza kuipora nyumba yake.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu anayeweza kuingia katika nyumba ya mtu mwenye nguvu na kuiba vitu vyake, isipokuwa kwanza amfunge yule mwenye nguvu. Baada ya hapo anaweza kuchukua kila kitu kilichomo nyumbani.

decisions.choice: the strong man is Satan; the one who binds him is Jesus
decisions.reason: Jesus is not in league with Satan; he has overpowered him. Freeing people from demons is carrying off Satan's goods. Isaiah 49:24-25 speaks of taking captives from the mighty.

decisions.choice: goods: household things, possessions
decisions.reason: The word means vessels or belongings. In the picture they are the people Satan holds.

decisions.choice: unless he first binds: Satan has already been overcome
alternatives: the binding is still to come
decisions.reason: Jesus' power over the demons shows that the strong man is already tied. Mark may point back to the testing in the wilderness (1:13).

decisions.choice: he (for the one who binds)
decisions.reason: The pronouns belong to a figure in a picture, so they take no deity_pronoun span, though the meaning note says the figure stands for Jesus.

decisions.choice: the "unless" clause comes before the main verb
alternatives: keeping the Greek order with a bracketed tail ("[그렇지 않으면]")
decisions.reason: Korean puts a condition before what it governs; the clause order changes but nothing is added.

decisions.choice: no pronoun for the one who binds; "người ấy" for the strong man
decisions.reason: Vietnamese can leave the subject unsaid, so "không ai ... nếu không trói" keeps the one who binds as open as the parable does and leaves "người ấy" for the strong man alone.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: In the picture, the one who binds the strong man stands for Jesus (meaning decision m1), but the pronouns belong to the figures of the saying, so they take no span, as in English.

source.text: Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πάντα ἀφεθήσεται τοῖς υἱοῖς τῶν ἀνθρώπων, τὰ ἁμαρτήματα καὶ αἱ βλασφημίαι ὅσα ἐὰν βλασφημήσωσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Truly I say to you that all will be forgiven to the sons of the men, the sins and the blasphemies, as many as they might blaspheme;

en.L: Truly I say to you that all things will be forgiven the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}, the sins and the blasphemies, however many they blaspheme;
en.B: Truly I tell you, {{gender:people|men}} will be forgiven all their sins and all the blasphemies they speak, however many they may be.
en.R: I tell you the truth: God will forgive people for every sin they do, and for every bad thing they say against God.

ko.L: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 사람의 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}이 짓는 모든 것, 곧 죄들과 모독들은, 그들이 얼마나 모독하든지 다 용서받을 것이다.
ko.B: 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 사람들이 짓는 모든 죄와 하나님을 모독하는 모든 말은, 아무리 많아도 용서받을 것이다.
ko.R: 내가 분명히 말한다. 사람들이 짓는 죄는 무엇이든, 또 하나님을 욕되게 하는 말은 무엇이든, 하나님께서 다 용서해 주실 것이다.

vi.L: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người rằng mọi sự sẽ được tha cho con cái loài người, các tội lỗi và các lời phạm thượng, bao nhiêu lời phạm thượng họ nói ra;
vi.B: Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các người: mọi tội lỗi của loài người đều sẽ được tha, kể cả mọi lời phạm thượng họ nói ra, dù nhiều đến đâu.
vi.R: Ta nói thật với các người: Đức Chúa Trời sẽ tha cho người ta mọi tội họ phạm, và mọi lời xấu xa họ nói nghịch cùng Đức Chúa Trời.

es.L: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que todo será perdonado a {{gender:los hijos de la humanidad|los hijos de los hombres}}, los pecados y las blasfemias, por muchas que pronuncien;
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que a {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} se les perdonarán todos sus pecados y todas las blasfemias que digan, por muchas que sean.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: Dios perdonará a las personas todos los pecados que cometan y todo lo malo que digan contra Dios.

fr.L: En vérité, je vous le dis : tout sera pardonné aux {{gender:enfants des humains|fils des hommes}}, les péchés et les blasphèmes, autant qu’ils en auront proféré ;
fr.B: En vérité, je vous le dis : {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} recevront le pardon de tous leurs péchés et de tous les blasphèmes qu’ils prononceront, si nombreux soient-ils.
fr.R: Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : Dieu pardonnera aux gens tous les péchés qu’ils commettent, et toutes les insultes qu’ils disent contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Kweli nawaambia kwamba wana wa watu watasamehewa yote, dhambi na makufuru, makufuru yoyote watakayoyatamka;
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, wanadamu watasamehewa dhambi zao zote na makufuru yao yote, hata yawe mengi namna gani.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: Mungu atawasamehe watu kila dhambi wanayotenda, na kila neno baya wanalosema dhidi ya Mungu.

decisions.choice: truly: a solemn opening, "amen"
alternatives: only agreement with something said before
decisions.reason: People said "amen" to agree with what another had said. Jesus puts it first, to stress what he is about to say. This is the first of many such sayings in Mark.

decisions.choice: the sons of men: human beings
decisions.reason: This Semitic phrase means people in general. The gender setting applies.

decisions.choice: blasphemies: words spoken against God
decisions.reason: As in 2:7. Even these can be forgiven.

decisions.choice: will be forgiven: God forgives
decisions.reason: The passive implies that God is the one who forgives.

decisions.choice: God will forgive
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as the single "amen" sayings in John.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R)
decisions.reason: As the single form of the Korean John's "진실로 진실로": Mark has one "amen". Modern endings replace the archaic "이르노니". Kept through Mark.

decisions.choice: {{gender:자녀들|아들들}} (L); "사람들" with no span (B, R)
alternatives: "사람의 아들들" at Literal with no span
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom "sons of men" and gives the inclusive form by default, as the Korean Colossians does; Balanced and Readable say "사람들", which already includes men and women, so the gender setting has nothing to change there.

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các người" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các người" (R) for the single "amen" (whole book)
decisions.reason: The Vietnamese John's form for the double "amen" ("Thật vậy, thật vậy"), said once, as Mark has it once. Jesus speaks to the scribes, so "các người", the form the style guide sets for opponents.

decisions.choice: "con cái loài người", with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Con cái" includes sons and daughters, so the English gender span has no Vietnamese counterpart (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The wording the Spanish of John uses for the double "amen", here with the single word. Jesus speaks to the scribes, so "you" is plural and takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: {{gender:los hijos de la humanidad|los hijos de los hombres}} (L); {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} (B)
decisions.reason: As in English: the idiom means human beings (meaning decision m2). Readable says "las personas", which is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: Mark has the single "amen" (meaning decision m1); French follows the wording set in John for the double one, with a single "en vérité".

decisions.choice: aux {{gender:enfants des humains|fils des hommes}} (L); {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} (B)
decisions.reason: The idiom means human beings (meaning decision m2). The default says it inclusively; the alternative keeps the traditional "fils des hommes" and "les hommes". Readable says "les gens" and needs no setting.

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's single "amen" is a solemn opening (m1). John's double amen is "Kweli kweli nawaambia"; the single one is "Kweli nawaambia", and Readable says "I tell you the truth" as in John. For the whole book.

decisions.choice: wana wa watu (L); wanadamu (B); watu (R), with no gender span
alternatives: a span with "wanaume" (males) as the alternative
decisions.reason: The English needs "children of humankind" with "sons of men" as the traditional alternative. Swahili "wana" (children, sons), "wanadamu" and "watu" already include men and women, and "wanaume" would mean males only and change the meaning, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

source.text: ὃς δ’ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ἁμαρτήματος.

records.literal_gloss: whoever but blasphemes against the Spirit the Holy, not has forgiveness to the age, but guilty is of eternal sin.

en.L: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin."
en.B: But anyone who blasphemes against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness, ever; that person is guilty of an eternal sin."
en.R: But anyone who says evil things against the Holy Spirit can never be forgiven. That person is guilty of an eternal sin, a sin that lasts forever."

ko.L: 그러나 누구든지 성령을 모독하는 사람은 영원히 용서를 받지 못하고, 영원한 죄에 대하여 책임을 진다."
ko.B: 그러나 성령을 모독하는 사람은 결코 용서받지 못하고, 영원한 죄를 짊어진다."
ko.R: 그러나 성령을 욕되게 하는 사람은 절대로 용서받지 못한다. 그 사람은 영원한 죄, 곧 영원히 남는 죄를 지은 것이다."

vi.L: nhưng ai phạm thượng đến Đức Thánh Linh thì không có sự tha thứ đến đời đời, mà phải mắc một tội đời đời."
vi.B: Nhưng ai phạm thượng đến Đức Thánh Linh thì không bao giờ được tha; người ấy mắc một tội đời đời."
vi.R: Nhưng ai nói xúc phạm Đức Thánh Linh thì sẽ không bao giờ được tha. Người ấy mắc một tội đời đời, một tội còn mãi mãi."

es.L: pero el que blasfeme contra el Espíritu Santo no tiene perdón jamás, sino que es culpable de un pecado eterno».
es.B: Pero el que blasfeme contra el Espíritu Santo no tendrá perdón jamás; es culpable de un pecado eterno».
es.R: Pero el que hable mal del Espíritu Santo nunca será perdonado. Esa persona es culpable de un pecado eterno, un pecado que dura para siempre».

fr.L: mais celui qui blasphème contre l’Esprit Saint n’a jamais de pardon, mais il est coupable d’un péché éternel. »
fr.B: Mais celui qui blasphème contre l’Esprit Saint n’obtiendra jamais de pardon : il est coupable d’un péché éternel. »
fr.R: Mais celui qui dit du mal de l’Esprit Saint ne pourra jamais être pardonné. Il est coupable d’un péché éternel, un péché qui ne finira jamais. »

sw.L: lakini yeyote atakayemkufuru Roho Mtakatifu hana msamaha milele, bali ana hatia ya dhambi ya milele."
sw.B: Lakini mtu yeyote atakayemkufuru Roho Mtakatifu hatasamehewa kamwe; mtu huyo ana hatia ya dhambi ya milele."
sw.R: Lakini mtu anayesema maneno mabaya dhidi ya Roho Mtakatifu hatasamehewa kamwe. Mtu huyo ana hatia ya dhambi ya milele, dhambi isiyokwisha kamwe."

decisions.choice: blaspheming the Holy Spirit: calling the Spirit's work the work of Satan
alternatives: any sin a believer fears is too great
decisions.reason: Mark explains in 3:30: they said that the power by which Jesus drives out demons was an unclean spirit. To call God's saving work evil is to refuse the only source of forgiveness.

decisions.choice: not to the age: never
alternatives: not in this age, but perhaps later
decisions.reason: "To the age" means forever.

decisions.choice: an eternal sin, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "eternal judgment", which is easier to understand. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: guilty of: held to account for
decisions.reason: The word is a legal one: liable to punishment for.

decisions.choice: a sin that lasts forever
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key word "eternal" and says what it means.

decisions.choice: "모독하다" (L, B); "욕되게 하다" (R) for blaspheme, here and in 3:28
decisions.reason: "모독" is the word of the Korean John (10:33-36) for speaking against God; Readable uses the plainer "욕되게 하다". "훼방하다" is the older church word.

decisions.choice: "phạm thượng" (L, B); "nói xúc phạm" (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese John (10:33): "phạm thượng" is the standard word; Readable says plainly what it is.

decisions.choice: hable mal del
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for "blaspheme": speaking evil against the Spirit.

decisions.choice: celui qui ... il, with no gender span
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets out, "celui qui" already means anyone, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French; the English "anyone ... that person" needs no span either.

source.text: ὅτι ἔλεγον· Πνεῦμα ἀκάθαρτον ἔχει.

records.literal_gloss: Because they were saying, A spirit unclean he has.

en.L: For they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
en.B: Jesus spoke this way because they were claiming, "He has an unclean spirit."
en.R: Jesus said this because the teachers of the law were saying, "He has an evil spirit in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

ko.L: 그들이 "그는 더러운 영이 들렸다" 하고 말하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서 이렇게 말씀하신 것은, 그들이 "그는 더러운 영이 들렸다" 하고 말했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 예수께서 이 말씀을 하신 것은, 율법학자들이 "저 사람 속에 악한 영이 들어 있다!" 하고 말했기 때문이다.

vi.L: Vì họ nói: "Ông ta có tà linh ô uế."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu nói như vậy vì họ cho rằng: "Ông ta bị tà linh ô uế ám."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói điều này vì các thầy dạy luật nói: "Ông ta bị tà linh ám."

es.L: Porque decían: «Tiene un espíritu impuro».
es.B: Jesús habló así porque ellos afirmaban: «Tiene un espíritu impuro».
es.R: Jesús dijo esto porque los maestros de la ley decían: «Tiene un espíritu malo dentro».

fr.L: Car ils disaient : « Il a un esprit impur. »
fr.B: Jésus parla ainsi parce qu’ils affirmaient : « Il a un esprit impur. »
fr.R: Jésus a dit cela parce que les spécialistes de la Loi disaient : « Il a un esprit mauvais en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. »

sw.L: Kwa sababu walikuwa wakisema, "Ana roho mchafu."
sw.B: Yesu alisema hivyo kwa sababu walikuwa wakidai, "Ana roho mchafu."
sw.R: Yesu alisema hivi kwa sababu walimu wa Sheria walikuwa wakisema, "Ana roho mwovu ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."

decisions.choice: because they were saying: Mark explains why Jesus said 3:29
decisions.reason: This is Mark's comment, not Jesus' speech.

decisions.choice: an unclean spirit: their charge in 3:22, said again
decisions.reason: They called the Holy Spirit at work in Jesus an unclean spirit.

decisions.choice: Jesus spoke this way because (B); Jesus said this because (R)
decisions.reason: English needs the link spelled out when a sentence begins with "because".

decisions.choice: the teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" were, the scribes of 3:22.

decisions.choice: "ông ta", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The accusers' words, as in 3:22: they speak of him as "ông ta".

decisions.choice: Tiene un espíritu malo dentro
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no pronoun for "in him", so the English span has no counterpart.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔξω στήκοντες ἀπέστειλαν πρὸς αὐτὸν καλοῦντες αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And come the mother of him and the brothers of him, and outside standing they sent to him calling him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} brothers come, and standing outside they sent to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, calling {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother and brothers arrived. They stood outside and sent word in, asking for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then Jesus' mother and brothers came to the house. They stood outside and sent someone in to call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 어머니와 그분의 형제들이 온다. 그리고 밖에 서서 그분께 사람을 보내어 그분을 불렀다.
ko.B: 그때 예수의 어머니와 형제들이 왔다. 그들은 밖에 서서 사람을 들여보내 예수를 불렀다.
ko.R: 그때 예수의 어머니와 형제들이 그 집에 왔다. 그들은 밖에 서서 사람을 들여보내 예수를 부르게 했다.

vi.L: Và mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, và đứng bên ngoài, họ sai người vào gọi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ mẹ và các anh em của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến. Họ đứng bên ngoài và nhờ người vào gọi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Rồi mẹ và các anh em của Đức Giê-xu đến ngôi nhà ấy. Họ đứng bên ngoài và nhờ một người vào gọi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

es.L: Y llegan {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos, y, de pie afuera, enviaron [a alguien] a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para llamarlo.
es.B: Entonces llegaron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} hermanos. Se quedaron afuera y mandaron a llamarlo.
es.R: Entonces llegaron a la casa la madre y los hermanos de Jesús. Se quedaron afuera y mandaron a alguien a llamarlo.

fr.L: Et viennent {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères, et, se tenant dehors, ils envoyèrent [quelqu’un] vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appeler.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} frères arrivèrent. Restés dehors, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} firent demander.
fr.R: Ensuite, la mère et les frères de Jésus sont arrivés à la maison. Ils sont restés dehors et ont envoyé quelqu’un {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}appeler.

sw.L: Na wanakuja mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, na wakisimama nje, wakatuma [ujumbe] {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, wakimwita.
sw.B: Kisha mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wakafika. Wakasimama nje, wakatuma ujumbe ndani, wakimwita.
sw.R: Kisha mama wa Yesu na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} wakafika kwenye nyumba ile. Wakasimama nje, wakamtuma mtu ndani kumwita.

decisions.choice: his brothers: brothers named in 6:3
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names James, Joses, Judas and Simon, and mentions sisters. Whether they were sons of Mary or relatives in some other sense was later debated; the text calls them brothers.

decisions.choice: his family arrives: the story begun in 3:21
decisions.reason: Mark frames the scribes' charge (3:22-30) with the family's coming (3:21, 31-35).

decisions.choice: standing outside: they are outside, the crowd is inside
decisions.reason: Mark sets those outside against those sitting around Jesus (3:34).

decisions.choice: "형제들", not "동생들"; no gender span
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John (2:12; 7:3): "동생들" would decide that they were younger brothers, which the text does not say. Specific men are meant, so there is no gender span.

decisions.choice: "anh em" for his brothers
decisions.reason: As in the Vietnamese John (2:12; 7:3): "anh em" names brothers without saying whether they are older or younger, which the meaning decision leaves open.

decisions.choice: [a alguien]
decisions.reason: Spanish "enviar" needs a person to send; the Greek leaves it implied.

decisions.choice: ses frères, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: Specific men are meant (meaning decision m1, 6:3), as for Jesus’s brothers in John 2:12.

source.text: καὶ ἐκάθητο περὶ αὐτὸν ὄχλος, καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ἰδοὺ ἡ μήτηρ σου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί σου ἔξω ζητοῦσίν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And was sitting around him a crowd, and they say to him, Behold, the mother of you and the brothers of you outside are seeking you.

en.L: And a crowd was sitting around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} brothers [are] outside, seeking {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.B: A crowd was sitting around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mother and brothers are outside, and they want {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: There was a crowd sitting around Jesus. They told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Your mother and your brothers are outside. They want to see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

ko.L: 그리고 무리가 그분 둘레에 앉아 있었는데, 그들이 그분께 말한다. "보십시오, 선생님의 어머니와 선생님의 형제들이 밖에서 선생님을 찾으십니다."
ko.B: 예수 둘레에는 무리가 앉아 있었는데, 그들이 예수께 말했다. "보십시오, 선생님의 어머니와 형제들이 밖에서 선생님을 찾으십니다."
ko.R: 예수 둘레에 많은 사람이 앉아 있었다. 그들이 예수께 말했다. "선생님의 어머니와 형제들이 밖에 와 계십니다. 선생님을 만나고 싶어 하십니다."

vi.L: Và đám đông ngồi quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Kìa, mẹ Thầy và anh em Thầy [đang] ở bên ngoài tìm Thầy."
vi.B: Đám đông đang ngồi quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, mẹ và anh em Thầy đang ở ngoài kia tìm Thầy."
vi.R: Có một đám đông ngồi quanh Đức Giê-xu. Họ nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Thầy, mẹ và các anh em của Thầy đang ở ngoài. Họ muốn gặp Thầy."

es.L: Y una multitud estaba sentada alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dicen: «Mira, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} hermanos afuera {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscan».
es.B: Había una multitud sentada alrededor de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Mira, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} hermanos están afuera y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscan».
es.R: Había mucha gente sentada alrededor de Jesús. Le dijeron: «Tu madre y {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} hermanos están afuera. Quieren verte».

fr.L: Et une foule était assise autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Voici, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} frères [sont] dehors, ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} cherchent. »
fr.B: Une foule était assise autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et on {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Écoute, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} frères sont dehors, ils {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demandent. »
fr.R: Il y avait une foule assise autour de Jésus. Des gens {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Ta mère et {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} frères sont dehors. Ils veulent {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} voir. »

sw.L: Na umati ulikuwa umeketi kumzunguka, nao wanamwambia, "Tazama, mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} [wako] nje, wanakutafuta."
sw.B: Umati wa watu ulikuwa umeketi kumzunguka, nao wakamwambia, "Tazama, mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} wako nje, wanakutaka."
sw.R: Kulikuwa na umati wa watu waliokuwa wameketi kumzunguka Yesu. Wakamwambia, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} wako nje. Wanataka kukuona."

decisions.choice: your mother and your brothers, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts add "and your sisters". The SBLGNT follows those that do not, in line with 3:31. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: seeking you: asking for you, wanting you
alternatives: looking for you, not knowing where you are
decisions.reason: They know where he is; they want him to come out.

decisions.choice: The crowd speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체 and says "선생님" for "you"
decisions.reason: Korean does not address a respected teacher as "you"; "선생님" stands for the pronoun, so Literal does not bracket it. The honorific "찾으십니다" honours his mother.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "you" and "your", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The crowd listening to him speak to him as their teacher. As the style guide sets, "Thầy" is a noun of address, always capitalised, and takes no span where the English has one.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} buscan (L, B); quieren verte (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "seek": they are asking for him (meaning decision m2).

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτοῖς λέγει· Τίς ἐστιν ἡ μήτηρ μου ἢ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου;

records.literal_gloss: And answering them he says, Who is the mother of me and the brothers of me?

en.L: And answering them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"
en.B: He answered, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother? Who are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers?"
en.R: Jesus answered, "Who is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} real family?"

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 그들에게 대답하여 말씀하신다. "누가 내 어머니이고 내 형제들이냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "누가 내 어머니이고, 누가 내 형제들이냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 대답하셨다. "누가 나의 진짜 가족이냐?"

vi.L: Và trả lời họ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Ai là mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"
vi.B: Ngài đáp: "Ai là mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? Ai là anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Ai mới thật là gia đình của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?"

es.L: Y respondiéndoles, dice: «¿Quién es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre y [quiénes son] {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos?».
es.B: Les respondió: «¿Quién es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre? ¿Y quiénes son {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos?».
es.R: Jesús respondió: «¿Quién es en realidad {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} familia?».

fr.L: Et, leur répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Qui est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère, et [qui sont] {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères ? »
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Qui est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère ? Qui sont {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères ? »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Qui est {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} vraie famille ? »

sw.L: Naye akiwajibu, anasema, "Ni nani mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} au ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}?"
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ni nani? Ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}} ni akina nani?"
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Familia {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} halisi ni akina nani?"

decisions.choice: who are my mother and brothers? a question that leads to the answer
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny his family. He asks the question to show who belongs to him in a deeper way (3:35).

decisions.choice: my real family
decisions.reason: Readable says what the question is about. The answer in 3:34-35 names mother and brothers.

decisions.choice: [quiénes son]
decisions.reason: The Greek has one singular verb for both; Spanish needs a plural verb for "brothers".

source.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος τοὺς περὶ αὐτὸν κύκλῳ καθημένους λέγει· Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ μου καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοί μου·

records.literal_gloss: And having looked around at those around him in a circle sitting, he says, Behold, the mother of me and the brothers of me.

en.L: And looking around at those sitting in a circle around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers!
en.B: He looked at the people sitting in a circle around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "See, these are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers!
en.R: Jesus looked at the people sitting around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He said, "These people are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brothers!

ko.L: 그리고 자기 둘레에 빙 둘러앉은 사람들을 둘러보시며 말씀하신다. "보아라, 내 어머니와 내 형제들이다.
ko.B: 그리고 자기 둘레에 둘러앉은 사람들을 둘러보시며 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 이 사람들이 내 어머니이고 내 형제들이다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 둘레에 앉아 있는 사람들을 둘러보시며 말씀하셨다. "이 사람들이 바로 내 어머니이고 내 형제들이다.

vi.L: Và nhìn quanh những người ngồi vòng quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Kìa, mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}!
vi.B: Ngài nhìn những người đang ngồi thành vòng quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Đây là mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}!
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nhìn những người đang ngồi quanh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài nói: "Những người này là mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và anh em {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}!

es.L: Y mirando alrededor a los que estaban sentados en círculo en torno a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, dice: «He aquí {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos.
es.B: Miró a los que estaban sentados en círculo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor y dijo: «¡Aquí están {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos!
es.R: Jesús miró a la gente que estaba sentada a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor y dijo: «¡Estas personas son {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} madre y {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} hermanos!

fr.L: Et, ayant regardé tout autour ceux qui étaient assis en cercle autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Voici {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères !
fr.B: Il regarda ceux qui étaient assis en cercle autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et dit : « Voici {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères !
fr.R: Jésus a regardé les gens assis autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il a dit : « Ces gens sont {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} mère et {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} frères !

sw.L: Naye akiisha kuwatazama pande zote wale walioketi kumzunguka, anasema, "Tazama, mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}!
sw.B: Akawatazama watu waliokuwa wameketi kumzunguka, akasema, "Tazameni, hawa ndio mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}!
sw.R: Yesu aliwatazama watu walioketi kumzunguka. Akasema, "Watu hawa ndio mama {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na ndugu {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}!

decisions.choice: looking around at those sitting around him: his disciples and the crowd who listen
decisions.reason: Those inside, sitting at his feet to listen, are set against those standing outside (3:31).

decisions.choice: my mother and my brothers: a new family around Jesus
alternatives: his own family is cast off
decisions.reason: Jesus names those who listen to him as his family. The bond is shown in 3:35.

decisions.choice: he aquí (L); aquí están (B); estas personas son (R)
decisions.reason: As in the Spanish of John: "he aquí" is formal but current, so Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable point in everyday words.

source.text: ὃς γὰρ ἂν ποιήσῃ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος ἀδελφός μου καὶ ἀδελφὴ καὶ μήτηρ ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever for does the will of the God, this one brother of me and sister and mother is.

en.L: For whoever does the will of God, this one is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brother and sister and mother."
en.B: Whoever does what God wants is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brother and sister and mother."
en.R: Anyone who does what God wants is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} brother, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sister, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mother."

ko.L: 누구든지 하나님의 뜻을 행하는 사람, 바로 그 사람이 내 형제이고 자매이고 어머니이기 때문이다."
ko.B: 누구든지 하나님의 뜻을 행하는 사람은 내 형제이고 자매이고 어머니이다."
ko.R: 누구든지 하나님께서 원하시는 일을 하는 사람이 바로 내 형제이고, 내 자매이고, 내 어머니이다."

vi.L: Vì ai làm theo ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời, người ấy là anh em và chị em và mẹ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: Ai làm theo ý muốn của Đức Chúa Trời, người ấy là anh em, chị em và mẹ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Ai làm điều Đức Chúa Trời muốn, người ấy là anh em của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chị em của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và mẹ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

es.L: Porque el que haga la voluntad de Dios, ese es {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hermano y hermana y madre».

decisions.choice: the will of God: what God wants done
decisions.reason: Doing the will of God means obeying him, as Jesus does (14:36).

decisions.choice: brother and sister and mother: anyone, man or woman, belongs to Jesus' family
decisions.reason: Jesus adds "sister", though only mother and brothers were mentioned. His family is open to all who do God's will.

decisions.choice: this one (L); no pronoun (B, R)
decisions.reason: "This one" includes men and women, as "brother and sister" shows, so no gender span is needed.

decisions.choice: "형제이고 자매이고 어머니"
decisions.reason: Modern endings replace the archaic "-요" list of familiar versions; "누구든지" already includes men and women, so no gender span is needed.

decisions.choice: "chị em" for "sister"
decisions.reason: Like "anh em", "chị em" names a sister without saying older or younger, which suits a saying about anyone who does God's will.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} repeated before each noun
decisions.reason: Spanish repeats the possessive when the nouns differ in gender; Literal keeps the Greek's single "my".

decisions.choice: [ma] sœur, [ma] mère (L)
decisions.reason: Greek has one "my" for all three nouns; French possessives agree with each noun, so Literal supplies the feminine "ma" in brackets.

decisions.choice: Toute personne qui (R)
decisions.reason: The saying includes men and women (meaning decision m2), and the list that follows names a sister and a mother; Readable makes that plain with "toute personne", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: ndugu (brother) beside dada (sister)
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" is the usual word for brothers (3:31-34) and can mean a sibling of either sex; set beside "dada" (sister) it reads as "brother". "Kaka" would add the sense of an elder brother, which the Greek does not have.
